dimensions.dimension: Historical Kerala / India reservoir and flood data, especially pre-2020 (Idukki, Idamalayar, Periyar basin)

confirmed_sources.name: National Water Data Portal (NWDP) CKAN API
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Open CKAN 2.x API over 555 datasets from CWC, CGWB and every state water department. No registration, no API key, no rate limit hit in ~40 calls. Endpoints used and verified: /api/3/action/package_list, /api/3/action/package_show?id=<slug>, /api/3/action/status_show. Resource CSVs are direct, unauthenticated downloads.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - this is the single highest-value new door for AquaSync; it is how you reach every Periyar gauge series below, and it can be wired into the existing data loader in a day
confirmed_sources.last_activity: live; Kerala and CWC resources carry 2026-2030 forward files, so it is actively maintained
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s 'https://nwdp.nwic.gov.in/api/3/action/package_show?id=river-discharge-manual-dailly-central-water-commission-cwc'
confirmed_sources.caveat: Dataset titles routinely lie about temporal coverage (see the Kerala SW discharge entry). Always download and histogram the date column before believing a title. The geographic hierarchy columns (River/Basin/Tributary) are corrupted by a bad join across the whole portal.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC Kerala daily river discharge 2001-2025 (NWDP resource)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 39,425,558 bytes, 217,538 rows, 40 Kerala CWC gauging stations. Periyar rows = 30,833. NEELEESWARAM 8,478 records 2001-2025 (284 in 2018); VANDIPERIYAR 14,837 (568 in 2018, twice-daily 08:00 and 08:30); ARANGALI 7,518 (173 in 2018). Columns include Station, Latitude, Longitude, 'Data Acquisition Time' (DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM), 'Manual Daily River Water Discharge (m3/sec)'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - genuine observed Periyar discharge covering 2018 and the whole pre-2020 period; the downstream validation target AquaSync currently has no observations for
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -L -A 'Mozilla/5.0' -o cwc_kl_2001.csv '<this url>'  (~90 s)
confirmed_sources.caveat: VERIFIED HOLE: Neeleeswaram August 2018 is missing days 5,12,16,17,18,19,20,21,22,24,25,26,27 - the flood peak (16-22 Aug) is entirely absent. Arangali is missing 16-27 Aug. Record density also decays: Neeleeswaram had 365 days in 2001-2004 but only 276-335 per year after 2023. Timestamps are single instantaneous readings, not daily means.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC Kerala daily river discharge 1950-2000 (NWDP resource)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 23,703,774 bytes, 134,069 rows. Periyar rows = 19,588. NEELEESWARAM 10,884 records starting 1971 (near-complete 365/yr 1972-1977, then 730/yr from 1978 as two readings per day); ARANGALI 8,276; VANDIPERIYAR 428.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - gives a 55-year continuous Periyar discharge record when joined to the 2001-2025 file; enough for flood-frequency, rating-curve and Muskingum work on long timescales
confirmed_sources.download_hint: same pattern as above; join on Station + parse 'Data Acquisition Time' as %d-%m-%Y %H:%M
confirmed_sources.caveat: Despite the '1950' in the filename, the earliest Periyar record is 1971. Deduplicate against the 2001-2025 file - year 2000 appears in both.

confirmed_sources.name: Kerala SW manual daily rainfall 1991-2020 (NWDP resource)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 24,200,224 bytes, 151,429 rows. Actual year span is 2000-2020 (not 1991). 2018 has 8,435 station-days. IDUKKI district 7,462 rows, ERNAKULAM 366. Long-record catchment stations: BOYCE ESTATE (9.56472,76.91056) 2000-2020, Vannapuram (9.93611,76.46333) 2002-2020.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - real gauge rainfall inside the Idukki catchment spanning 2018, to force the existing SCS-CN model and to bias-check IMD gridded
confirmed_sources.last_activity: companion 2021-2025 and 2026-2030 resources exist in the same package
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -L -A 'Mozilla/5.0' -o rf_kerala.csv '<this url>'
confirmed_sources.caveat: Titled 1991-2020, actually starts 2000. Only 2 of the 7 Idukki/Ernakulam stations have multi-year records - Neriyamangalam and Boothathankettu (the Periyar main-stem stations) exist for 2011 ONLY. River/Basin columns are wrong (Kerala stations labelled 'Tapi', 'Balki').

confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Advertised as 'River Discharge Kerala_SW Kerala (2001 - 2025) Manual Daily'. Actually 765,060 bytes, 4,904 rows, ALL from calendar year 2011, 23 stations, ZERO Periyar rows.

confirmed_sources.name: RAT 3.0 Kerala live dashboard (CWRDM + UW SASWE + NASA)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Satellite + VIC reservoir monitoring for 19 Kerala reservoirs including Idukki (9.845,76.968) and Idamalayaar (10.222,76.706). Products per dam: inflow, outflow, area-elevation curve, TMS-OS surface area, storage change (dels), evaporation. Served as plain static CSVs, no auth.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the only downloadable daily Idukki/Idamalayar inflow series that spans 2018, plus a free area-elevation curve to sanity-check AquaSync's level-storage power law
confirmed_sources.license: not stated on the portal; RAT engine itself is GPL-3.0
confirmed_sources.last_activity: data ends 2025-02-22, so the Kerala instance is ~18 months stale as of Aug 2026
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Dam list: curl 'http://210.212.226.241:8080/RAT_Kerala_CWRDM/assets/map_data/dam_locations.csv'  then per-dam: /assets/RAT_results/{inflow|outflow|aec|sarea_tmsos|dels|evaporation}/{idukki|idamalayaar}.csv

confirmed_sources.name: RAT Kerala - Idukki daily inflow CSV
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 100,264 bytes, 3,410 daily rows, columns date,streamflow (m3/s), 2015-10-24 to 2025-02-22, unbroken. August 2018 complete (31/31 days). Idamalayar twin at .../inflow/idamalayaar.csv, same span.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - directly fills 'no pre-2020 Idukki data' as a MODELLED series; usable as a prior or for antecedent-moisture initialisation, not as ground truth
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -o rat_idukki_inflow.csv 'http://210.212.226.241:8080/RAT_Kerala_CWRDM/assets/RAT_results/inflow/idukki.csv'
confirmed_sources.caveat: VERIFIED MISMATCH at the event that matters: RAT Aug-2018 peak 1104.6 m3/s on the 18th vs CWC-observed 2532 cumec at 22:00 on the 15th (2.3x low, 3 days late). RAT gives only 309.9 m3/s on 15 Aug when CWC reports a 1640 cumec daily-average inflow. This is VIC output forced by IMERG, uncalibrated for Idukki (Mullaperiyar transfers upstream are unmodelled in the plain series). Published Idukki skill is r=0.63, RMSE 217.9 m3/s.

confirmed_sources.name: RAT Kerala - Idukki area-elevation curve (AEC)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 626 rows at 1 m elevation steps, 551 m to 1176 m, columns elevation,area(km2). Idukki: 50.015 km2 @730 m, 51.098 @731, 52.125 @732, 53.201 @733. Idamalayar twin has 588 rows, 62-649 m: 30.159 @167, 30.414 @168, 30.666 @169 (FRL).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - an independent hypsometric curve to cross-validate AquaSync's r2=0.9957 level-storage power law, and to convert satellite surface area into storage
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -o aec_idukki.csv '.../assets/RAT_results/aec/idukki.csv'
confirmed_sources.caveat: DEM-derived, and it disagrees with the literature at FRL: it gives 52.1 km2 at 732 m whereas Suresh et al. 2024 Table 1 lists Idukki as 60 km2 at FRL - roughly 13% low. Idamalayar is the opposite sign (30.7 km2 vs 28.3 km2 published, ~8% high). Rescale before use; do not adopt it as an absolute.

confirmed_sources.name: RAT Kerala - Idukki TMS-OS surface area and storage change
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 657 rows 2017-07-29 to 2025-02-21 (85 observations in 2018), columns date,area (km2). Paired storage change at /dels/idukki.csv, columns date,dS (m3). Optical (MNDWI/NDWI) fused with SAR.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - real satellite observation of Idukki through 2018, but see caveat; more trustworthy in the dry season than the monsoon
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -o sarea_idukki.csv '.../assets/RAT_results/sarea_tmsos/idukki.csv'
confirmed_sources.caveat: THE AUGUST 2018 VALUES ARE NOT REAL OBSERVATIONS. Area reads 46.2 km2 on 12 Aug then an identical 44.373 km2 on 17, 22 AND 27 Aug - a carried-forward value under monsoon cloud. It also implies the reservoir SHRANK while CWC records it filling to FRL 732.43 m at 01:00 on 17 Aug. The paired dels shows a spurious -102.8 Mm3 on 17 Aug. The RAT paper itself flags 'perennial high cloud cover' as the core limitation. Discard Idukki monsoon-2018 surface area.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC Reservoir Level & Storage Bulletin archive
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Weekly (Thursday) PDF bulletins covering 161 major Indian reservoirs, Idukki and Idamalayar among them. Per-reservoir fields: FRL (m), live capacity (BCM), bulletin date, current level (m), current live storage (BCM), % of capacity, same-week-last-year %, 10-year-average %, irrigation benefit (000 ha), installed hydropower (MW). Paginated ?page=0..~25; page 20 still lists April 2015.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the only official numeric Idukki level+storage series I could actually retrieve for 2018, and the only one that also carries Idamalayar
confirmed_sources.license: Government of India, free to reuse
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Scrape pages 11-16 for 2018: curl -s 'https://cwc.gov.in/en/reservoir-level-storage-bulletin?page=13' | grep -o 'href="[^"]*\.pdf"'  - then pypdf + regex 'IDUKKI\s+([\d.]+)\s+([\d.]+)\s+([\d.]+)\s+([\d.]+)'
confirmed_sources.caveat: Weekly only - far too coarse to constrain a flood-routing model. Filenames are wildly inconsistent (DD.MM.YYYYcwcbull.pdf, ..._1.pdf, ..._0.pdf, cwcbulletinDD.MM.YYYY.pdf, DD.MM.YYYYcwc.pdf), so you must scrape the listing, not construct URLs. 7 of 52 weeks of 2018 are absent including BOTH flood-week bulletins (09 and 16 Aug 2018) - I tried 7 filename variants, all 404.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC weekly bulletin, 02 August 2018 (worked example)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 539,052 bytes. Verified extracted row: 'IDUKKI 732.43 730.25 1.460 1.338 01-08-2018 92 23 41 - 780' = FRL 732.43 m, level 730.25 m, live cap 1.460 BCM, live storage 1.338 BCM, 92% full, 23% same week last year, 41% ten-year average, 780 MW. Sister bulletins verified: 23.08.2018 -> 731.69 m / 1.417 BCM / 97%; 30.08.2018 -> 730.50 m / 1.352 BCM / 93%.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - concrete proof the 2018 Idukki level/storage numbers are retrievable, and the FRL and 1.460 BCM live capacity independently confirm AquaSync's constants
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -o b.pdf 'https://cwc.gov.in/sites/default/files/02.08.2018cwcbull_1.pdf' && python -c "from pypdf import PdfReader; import re; t='\n'.join(p.extract_text() for p in PdfReader('b.pdf').pages); print(re.search(r'IDUKKI.{0,180}',t).group())"
confirmed_sources.caveat: Idukki appears twice per bulletin in two different table layouts (state table and the 161-reservoir national table) - anchor your regex or you will silently parse the wrong column order.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC 'Kerala Floods of August 2018' study report (via KSDMA)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 48 pages, 6,003,314 bytes. THE primary source (it is reference 4 of the Current Science paper). Verified quantitative content: Idukki peak inflow 2532 cumec at 22:00 on 15-08-2018; release 1614 cumec (1500 spill + 114 powerhouse); level 730.88 m at 18:00 on 14-08-2018; FRL 732.43 m reached 01:00 on 17-08-2018; peak attenuated 2532 -> 1500 cumec (~41%); 15-17 Aug totals 345 MCM spill + 30 MCM powerhouse against 435 MCM inflow, 60 MCM absorbed; Neeleswaram observed flood peak ~8800 cumec; Idamalayar live storage 1018 MCM, level 168.06 m on 08-08-2018, FRL 169.0 m, MWL 170.3 m, only 60 MCM of flood space; Idamalayar peak release 1272 cumec; design floods 5013 cumec (Idukki) and 3012 cumec (Idamalayar).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the authoritative 2018 numbers, and the correct calibration/validation targets for any AquaSync 2018 replay
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -o cwc2018.pdf '<this url>' ; pypdf extracts 72,025 chars of clean text
confirmed_sources.caveat: Fig.4 (Idukki inflow/outflow/level) and Fig.5 (Idamalayar) are CHARTS - there is no data table and no annexure. BUT the x-axis tick labels extract as PDF text (09-08-18 12:00 ... 18-08-18 06:00 at 7-hour steps), proving it is a vector Excel plot, so the series are recoverable by SVG path extraction (pdftocairo -svg) rather than pixel digitising. That is the cheapest realistic path to a 2018 hourly Idukki hydrograph.

confirmed_sources.name: Sudheer et al. 2019, 'Role of dams on the floods of August 2018 in Periyar River Basin, Kerala', Current Science 116(5):780-794
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Free full PDF, 15 pages, 4,413,605 bytes. HEC-HMS reconstruction of the whole Periyar basin. Verified numbers: simulated Idukki peak inflow 2763 m3/s at 20:00 on 15-08-2018 vs measured 2532 m3/s; simulated max release 1860 vs measured 1614 m3/s at 22:00; at L2 (= the Neeleeswaram CWC site) simulated 9965 vs observed 8800 m3/s; virgin (no-dam) simulation gives 8224 m3/s at L1 and 11,990 m3/s at L2; only 16-21% peak attenuation achievable by pre-emptying. Table 1 lists 14 Periyar dams with type, completion year, length and height.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the closest published analogue to what AquaSync's optimiser does, and its 16-21% attenuation ceiling is the number AquaSync's policy search should be benchmarked against
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -o cs0780.pdf 'https://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/116/05/0780.pdf'
confirmed_sources.caveat: NO DATA TABLE of any hydrograph. The observed 6-hourly Idukki inflow/release appears only inside Fig.6a and is cited to the CWC report. The paper acknowledges KSEB and CWRDM Kottayam supplied the underlying data - it does not redistribute it.

confirmed_sources.name: Suresh et al. 2024, RSE - free full manuscript on NASA NTRS
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 56 pages, 3,714,034 bytes - the accepted manuscript of the paywalled Remote Sensing of Environment paper (DOI 10.1016/j.rse.2024.114149), free. Contains the full 19-reservoir table with coordinates and FRL surface areas (Idukki 60 km2, Idamalayaar 28.3 km2), Table 4 inflow validation (Idukki r=0.63, RMSE 217.94 cumecs, nRMSE 12.45%; Idamalayaar r=0.81, RMSE 135.29; Kakki r=0.83; Banasurasagar r=0.78) and Table 5 (Idukki May-Oct 2018 vs KSEB observed: VIC r=0.80/RMSE 170.3/MAE 115.1/KGE 0.59/NSE 0.603; ResORR-regulated r=0.84/RMSE 153.17/MAE 102.32/KGE 0.63/NSE 0.68).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - gives the exact, citable error bars for the RAT inflow series AquaSync would ingest, and documents that KSEB holds and shares observed 2018 Idukki inflow
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -o suresh2024.pdf 'https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20240007715/downloads/Manuscript_RSE_Revised_03262024_clean.pdf'
confirmed_sources.caveat: Accepted manuscript, so figure numbering may differ slightly from the published version. The observed KSEB series it validates against is NOT included as a supplement - only the statistics are published.

confirmed_sources.name: Minocha et al. 2024, 'Reservoir Assessment Tool version 3.0', Geoscientific Model Development 17:3137
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Open-access description of the RAT 3.0 software platform: VIC hydrological model + MetSim + routing, IMERG forcing, TMS-OS surface area, GEE backend. Crossref-verified: published 2024-04-23, 6 citations.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the method paper you need if AquaSync ever runs its own RAT instance over the Periyar rather than consuming CWRDM's stale CSVs
confirmed_sources.download_hint: PDF at https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/17/3137/2024/gmd-17-3137-2024.pdf
confirmed_sources.caveat: Software paper, contains no Kerala data itself.

confirmed_sources.name: UW-SASWE/RAT (Reservoir Assessment Tool source)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Python implementation of RAT 3.0 - VIC + MetSim + routing + Google Earth Engine surface-area extraction, producing inflow, outflow, storage change, evaporation and AEC per reservoir.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - running it yourself over the Periyar with IMD rather than IMERG forcing, and with Mullaperiyar transfers represented, would plausibly beat the r=0.63 Idukki inflow that CWRDM publishes
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Docs at https://rat-satellitedams.readthedocs.io/ (200); global instance at https://www.satellitedams.net/ (200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Only 26 stars and GPL-3.0, which is a licence constraint if AquaSync ships closed. Heavy stack: needs a Google Earth Engine service account plus VIC/MetSim compiled. Realistically a week to a first Periyar run, not a day.

confirmed_sources.name: IMD 0.25-degree daily gridded rainfall - direct POST endpoint
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The form action behind the IMD download page. POST body RF25=<year> returns one NetCDF per year. VERIFIED LIVE: RF25=2018 gave HTTP 200, 25,431,832 bytes, CDF-1 classic NetCDF, variables LONGITUDE(135), LATITUDE(129), TIME(365, 'days since 1900-12-31'), RAINFALL(365,129,135) in mm. Grid 6.5-38.5N, 66.5-100.0E at 0.25 deg. Years 1901-2024.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the long-record rainfall forcing AquaSync's SCS-CN model needs for any pre-2020 replay; free, instant, no account
confirmed_sources.license: IMD open data (cite Pai et al. 2014)
confirmed_sources.last_activity: extended annually; 2024 is the latest full year
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -X POST -d 'RF25=2018' https://www.imdpune.gov.in/cmpg/Griddata/RF25.php -o RF25_2018.nc   # then scipy.io.netcdf_file, cell (9.75N, 77.00E) is nearest Idukki
confirmed_sources.caveat: 0.25 deg is ~28 km - the Idukki catchment (~1240 km2 incl. free catchment) is only a handful of cells, so orographic gradients across the Western Ghats are smeared. Verified Aug-2018 at the Idukki cell: 203.5 mm on the 9th, 153.3 and 201.8 mm on the 15th-16th, annual total 4048.9 mm. Missing values are coded -999; mask before summing.

confirmed_sources.name: GUARDIAN: ExtendinG SUb-DAily River Discharge data over INdia (Scientific Data, 2024)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Hourly (monsoon Jun-Sep) and sub-daily (non-monsoon) discharge for 210 CWC stations, 2020 to present, built by scraping water-surface elevation off the CWC flood portal and applying station rating curves. >800,000 discharge points per year, >4,000 per station per year. Crossref-verified 2024-10-18, 5 citations.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the practical answer to AquaSync gap #2 (Muskingum K and x never gauge-calibrated); hourly Neeleeswaram from 2020 overlaps the amith-vp KSEB release feed exactly
confirmed_sources.download_hint: See the figshare entry below for the actual files
confirmed_sources.caveat: STARTS 2020 - it does nothing for the 2018 gap. Discharge is rating-curve-derived, not measured, so it inherits rating error (Neeleeswaram monsoon NSE only 0.765, RMSE 170.7 m3/s).

confirmed_sources.name: GUARDIAN data on figshare (data.rar + rating curves)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Two files, confirmed via the figshare API (article 27004282, published 2024-10-19): data.rar 577.0 MB (extended WSE + extended discharge per station) and RC.xlsx 0.1 MB (rating curves). I downloaded RC.xlsx (53,652 bytes, 211 rows) and confirmed all three Periyar gauges: NEELEESWARAM (10.18361,76.49556) monsoon cubic-poly p1=10.6979 p2=198.7671 p3=33.5397, NSE 0.7654, RMSE 170.69, N=2273; non-monsoon p1=6.7636 p2=228.9940 p3=-36.1573, NSE 0.7861, RMSE 127.51, N=6552. ARANGALI monsoon NSE 0.9218 RMSE 42.10. VANDIPERIYAR power-law form, monsoon NSE 0.9476 RMSE 4.04.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the rating curves alone (0.1 MB) let AquaSync convert any CWC stage reading to Periyar discharge, and the 577 MB archive gives hourly Neeleeswaram hydrographs for Muskingum fitting
confirmed_sources.license: figshare API reports no licence field set - clarify before redistributing
confirmed_sources.download_hint: RC only (small): curl -L -o RC.xlsx https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/49150798 ; full archive: curl -L -o data.rar https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/49150774
confirmed_sources.caveat: HTTP 202 is figshare's normal async-landing response, not an error - the ndownloader links return 200. Archive is .rar, needs unrar/7z. VANDIPERIYAR's coordinates here (9.1525,77.1525) DISAGREE with the CWC NWDP file (9.57333,77.09056) by ~46 km - resolve before joining the two sources.

confirmed_sources.name: GHI: Geospatial dataset for hydrologic analyses in India (ESSD 15:4389, 2023)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Quality-controlled CWC river gauges with catchment boundaries and hydrometeorological time series over 71 water years (1950-2020). Of 645 CWC stations screened: 213 Group-1 (reliable metadata + adequate daily streamflow), 259 Group-2, 173 rejected. Explicitly mentions the Periyar River and the West-Flowing-Rivers-South basin (coastal Kerala). Crossref-verified 2023-10-05, 17 citations.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - delineated catchment polygons for the Periyar CWC gauges would let AquaSync define Muskingum reaches and SCS-CN sub-catchments on a published basis rather than by geometry estimate
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Data DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7563599 - see caveat
confirmed_sources.caveat: The data itself is on Zenodo, which returned 403 'unusual traffic from your network' for EVERY Zenodo URL I tried from this machine. The paper page is readable; the download needs a different network or a mirror. Also I could NOT confirm Neeleeswaram is in the 213-station Group 1 without opening the archive - verify before relying on it.

confirmed_sources.name: CAMELS-IND (ESSD 17:461, 2025)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 472 Peninsular-India catchments (228 with observed streamflow for >30% of 1980-2020), 1 Jan 1980 - 31 Dec 2020 daily. 19 meteorological forcings (precip, tmax/tmin, LW/SW radiation, U/V wind, RH, canopy and soil evaporation, actual and potential ET, soil moisture at 4 depths to 3 m), observed streamflow where available, plus LSTM-predicted streamflow for all 472. Catchment attributes include number of dams, dam volume, population density, urban/agri land-cover change. Crossref-verified 2025-02-05, 23 citations. Built on CWC gauges from India-WRIS using GHI catchment boundaries.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium-high - a ready large-sample training set if AquaSync attacks gap #3 (perfect-foresight assumption) with a learned inflow forecaster; the LSTM benchmark is a fair baseline to beat
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Data DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14005378
confirmed_sources.caveat: Zenodo returned 403 from this network for every attempt (doi.org redirect, /records/, and the /api/records/ JSON endpoint), so I could NOT open the archive to confirm which - if any - Periyar catchments are included. The paper says 'Peninsular India' and 15 CWC interstate basins, which includes Kerala's west-flowing rivers, but names no Kerala catchment. Ends 2020, so it does not carry 2018 Idukki operations - only catchment-scale forcing and streamflow.

confirmed_sources.name: Mishra et al., 'The Kerala flood of 2018: combined impact of extreme rainfall and reservoir storage' (HESS Discussions preprint)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Open preprint with full PDF. Establishes that 1-15 day August 2018 rainfall upstream of Idukki, Kakki and Periyar reservoirs had >500-year return periods, and that 6 of 7 major Kerala reservoirs were above 90% of capacity on 8 August 2018. States that Idukki reservoir storage for 2018 was obtained from India-WRIS for 1 Jan - 8 Aug 2018 only.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - useful for antecedent-condition framing and it independently confirms India-WRIS once served daily Idukki storage back to at least 2018
confirmed_sources.last_activity: 2018 preprint; remained in Discussions, not a final HESS paper
confirmed_sources.download_hint: PDF: https://hess.copernicus.org/preprints/hess-2018-480/hess-2018-480.pdf (verified 200)

confirmed_sources.name: India-WRIS API contract, recovered from WRIS_India_data_extractor source
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Flask app that wraps the undocumented India-WRIS endpoints. Reading the source gives the complete, otherwise-undocumented contract: POST https://indiawris.gov.in/DataSet/DataSetList ; POST /masterState/StateList {datasetcode} ; POST /masterDistrict/getDistrictbyState {statecode,datasetcode} ; POST /basin/getMasterBasin {datasetcode} ; POST /masterTributary/getMasterTributary {basincode,datasetcode} ; POST /masterAgency/AgencyListInAnyCase ; and the data calls POST /Dataset/{Name}?agencyName=&stateName=&districtName= or POST /Dataset/Basin/{Name}?agencyName=&basinName=&tributaryName= with body {startdate,enddate,size:1000,download:true,page:N}. Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded; Referer https://indiawris.gov.in/dataSet/ required; dataset names are URL-encoded with special cases 'RainFall', 'River%20WaterLevel', 'SnowFall'. No API key, no registration.

confirmed_sources.download_hint: gh api repos/DVTanna369/WRIS_India_data_extractor/contents/main_app/routes.py --jq .content | base64 -d

confirmed_sources.name: GloLakes: water storage dynamics for 27,000 lakes, 1984-present (ESSD 16:201, 2024)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Relative and absolute water storage time series from radar altimetry (Topex/Poseidon, Jason-1/2/3, Sentinel-3/6), ICESat-2 laser altimetry and Landsat/Sentinel-2 optical, 1984 to present. Crossref-verified 2024-01-11, 46 citations - the most-cited global reservoir storage dataset found.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - a genuinely independent satellite storage series that spans 2018, worth cross-checking against RAT and the CWC bulletins IF Idukki is among the 27,000
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Data DOI 10.25914/K8ZF-6G46 -> resolves 200 to NCI Australia GeoNetwork (geonetwork.nci.org.au)
confirmed_sources.caveat: I could NOT confirm Idukki or Idamalayar are in the 27,000 - the NCI GeoNetwork landing page is a JS catalogue and I did not open the archive. Radar altimetry needs a satellite ground track over the lake; Idukki is a narrow, steep-sided arch-dam reservoir (~52-60 km2) in mountainous terrain, which is exactly the geometry altimetry handles worst. Treat as unverified for these two dams.

confirmed_sources.name: Global Reservoir Surface Area Dataset (GRSAD)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Monthly Landsat-derived surface area for 6,817 global reservoirs (GRanD-matched) with cloud/shadow/SLC-off contamination repaired. March 1984 - October 2015.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - ENDS OCTOBER 2015, so it cannot see 2018 at all; listed only to close the question
confirmed_sources.last_activity: static; superseded by GloLakes and ReaLSAT
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Texas Data Repository (Dataverse) UI download
confirmed_sources.caveat: Hard stop at 2015-10 makes it useless for the 2018 event. Monthly resolution is in any case far too coarse for flood routing. Its only AquaSync value would be a long pre-2015 Idukki area baseline to extend the RAT AEC calibration.

confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Kerala State Disaster Management Authority's daily water-level page for major KSEB and Irrigation dams; also hosts the mirrored CWC 2018 flood report and a /floods_2018/ section (verified 200).
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - KSDMA is the institutional owner and the most likely formal counterparty for a data request; the site itself is the mirror that makes the CWC 2018 report freely reachable
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Companion pages verified 200: /water-level-status-in-dams/, /floods_2018/, /dam-management/

CWRDM Kottayam Sub Centre (Dr George Abe) is separately acknowledged in Sudheer et al. 2019 as the supplier of historic rainfall data, which corroborates that this is a working channel.

dead end: NWDP HAS NO KERALA RESERVOIR LEVEL OR STORAGE DATA AT ALL. I enumerated all 555 packages. Of 70 'reservoir' packages, 62 are reservoir_discharge_*_telemetry_hourly for individual dams in MP, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Telangana, UP, WB, Uttarakhand and Punjab - not one is in Kerala. The only reservoir level/storage packages are for Andhra Pradesh, BBMB Chandigarh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, and a CWC one. I opened the CWC package (reservoir-water-level-manual-daily-centre-water-commission_cwc): its 4 resources are Odisha storage and Madhya Pradesh water level ONLY. So Idukki and Idamalayar level/storage are definitively NOT on NWDP in any form.
