dimensions.dimension: Open-source reservoir operation, optimisation and forecast-informed operations (FIRO)

confirmed_sources.name: rtc-tools/rtc-tools (GitHub)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The RTC-Tools framework: goal programming, ensemble/scenario-tree optimisation (ControlTreeMixin), Modelica-based system modelling on CasADi. 16,410 lines of Python in src/. 15 shipped examples including single_reservoir, ensemble, pumped_hydropower_system, cascading_channels. Solver-agnostic (CBC, HiGHS, Ipopt open; Gurobi, CPLEX, Knitro commercial).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - closest thing to a production-grade open reservoir MPC framework; its goal-programming ladder and ControlTreeMixin directly address AquaSync's flood-vs-energy tradeoff and perfect-foresight gap
confirmed_sources.last_activity: 2026-08-26 (pushed same day checked); 1,496 commits, 18 contributors, 61 open issues
confirmed_sources.download_hint: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/rtc-tools/rtc-tools.git   (note: github.com/Deltares/rtc-tools, also 200, 301-redirects here). Governance page: https://lfenergy.org/projects/rtc-tools/ (200) - Deltares contributed it to LF Energy in 2025.
confirmed_sources.caveat: 24 stars understates it (LF Energy project with Deltares commercial backing) but does mean a thin community for troubleshooting. I verified EVERY optimisation example imports ModelicaMixin - there is no Python-only optimisation model API.

confirmed_sources.name: rtc-tools on PyPI
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Version 2.8.0 (2026-07-08), requires-python >=3.10, 88 releases. Declared deps: casadi!=3.6.6,<3.8,>=3.6.3, defusedxml>=0.7.0, numpy>=1.21.2, pymoca==0.9.*, rtc-tools-channel-flow>=1.2.0, rtc-tools-standard-library>=0.1.2, scipy>=1.7.2.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - I used this to MEASURE the real dependency burden rather than guessing at it
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install rtc-tools   (VERIFIED: installs exactly 9 packages - rtc-tools 2.8.0, casadi 3.7.2, pymoca 0.9.3, rtc-tools-channel-flow 1.3.1, rtc-tools-standard-library 0.1.2, numpy 2.5.2, scipy 1.18.1, defusedxml 0.7.1, antlr4-python3-runtime 4.13.2 - Windows/Python 3.12). Shipped single_reservoir example then ran in 3.07 s wall, 0.015 s in IPOPT.
confirmed_sources.caveat: Pins casadi<3.8 while CasADi is at 3.8.0, and pymoca==0.9.* while pymoca is at 0.12.0. Install still clean. The readthedocs Getting Started page (also 200) never mentions solvers - I established empirically that CasADi bundles IPOPT, Bonmin, HiGHS, CBC, Clp and qpOASES, which is why no separate solver build is needed.

confirmed_sources.name: Robust-FIRO (Taylor & Herman, UC Davis)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: MPCProblem.py - a 194-line cvxpy receding-horizon ensemble MPC for reservoir flood control. Also train_EFO.py (risk-threshold Ensemble Forecast Operations policy search), model.py (13 KB simple mass-balance reservoir), ecrps_functions.py (ensemble CRPS forecast verification), and a Cumulative Method baseline. Deps: numpy, pandas, xarray, scipy, cvxpy.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - THE most useful artefact in this dimension; the concrete answer to the perfect-foresight weakness, and its parameters (TOCS, ramp_rate, u_max) map 1:1 onto AquaSync's existing (target level, start hour, max rate) search
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wltaylor/Robust-FIRO/main/MPCProblem.py   (the whole formulation is in create_cvx(), ~30 lines)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Paper-support code, not a library: 1 star, no packaging, no tests, hard-coded to Oroville. `import mosek` at module level, and a solver-dispatch bug (if/if-else instead of elif) means a MOSEK run solves twice. I VERIFIED it works without MOSEK: ported to Idukki scale (1459 Mm3, 40 members x 14-day lead), 45 solves in 0.39 s at 8.8 ms/solve, status 'optimal', on free CLARABEL. Full reproduction needs Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15041287, which returns 403 to curl.

confirmed_sources.name: SSJRB-FIRO-Publishing (Taylor & Herman)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Multi-reservoir FIRO across the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Basin. Contains perfect_forecast.py (an explicit perfect-foresight baseline - exactly AquaSync's current assumption, isolated so the gap can be measured), train_firo.py (risk-threshold policy training), simulate_baseline_tocs.py, simulate_loocv.py and loocv.py (leave-one-out cross-validation of forecast-informed policies).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the perfect_forecast.py vs simulate_firo.py pairing is the exact experimental design AquaSync needs to quantify how much its optimiser loses once foresight is removed
confirmed_sources.caveat: 1 star, research code, California-specific data. Value is the experimental design and LOOCV validation pattern, not runnable-as-is software.

confirmed_sources.name: zpb4/syn-forecast_stochastic (Brodeur)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Synthetic hydrology and synthetic ensemble-forecast generation plus a FIRO model for Lake Oroville, supporting a manuscript on FIRO under climate extremes and evolving forecast skill.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - AquaSync has NO operational ensemble forecast feed for Kerala; this is the method for manufacturing statistically realistic synthetic forecast ensembles from a historical record, the missing input to the FIRO MPC
confirmed_sources.caveat: 1 star, 196 KB. Companion R repo zpb4/FIRO_synthetic-ensemble-forecasts (verified 200, 0 stars, no licence, 2024-01) implements the earlier WRR method. Research code both ways.

confirmed_sources.name: Lake Mendocino FIRO Final Viability Assessment (Dec 2020)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The primary published FVA for the flagship deployed FIRO programme; basis for USACE approving FIRO-based operations at Coyote Valley Dam. Produced by Sonoma Water + CW3E/Scripps with federal, state and local partners.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the authoritative precedent for arguing forecast-informed operation to a regulator like KSEB/KSDMA, and it documents the institutional pathway (virtual trials -> major deviations -> water control manual update) directly analogous to what AquaSync needs in Kerala
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -L -o LakeMendocino_FIRO_FVA.pdf https://cw3e.ucsd.edu/FIRO_docs/LakeMendocino_FIRO_FVA.pdf . One-page summary also verified 200: https://cw3e.ucsd.edu/FIRO_docs/LakeMendocino_FIRO_FVA_OnePageSummary.pdf
confirmed_sources.caveat: The commonly-cited eScholarship mirror (escholarship.org/uc/item/3b63q04n) returns 403 to curl - use this CW3E PDF. Contains no code. Outcomes: WY2019/WY2020 major deviations; WY2020 gave a 19% storage increase (>11,000 acre-feet); FIRO now authorised in the USACE Water Control Manual.

confirmed_sources.name: Prado Dam FIRO Final Viability Assessment
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The second completed FVA. Prado FIRO confirmed viable (2023), implementation ongoing including a water control manual update; reported benefit up to 23,000 acre-feet of additional recharge in wet years.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - second precedent, and structurally different from Mendocino (groundwater recharge rather than water supply), useful for showing FIRO generalises across objectives
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Companion work plan also verified 200: https://cw3e.ucsd.edu/FIRO_docs/Prado_Dam_work_plan.pdf
confirmed_sources.caveat: No code. Policy/engineering document only.

confirmed_sources.name: CW3E FIRO programme portal
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Index of the six FIRO programmes: Howard A. Hanson Dam, Prado Dam, Russian River Watershed, Seven Oaks Dam, Willamette Valley, Yuba & Feather Watersheds. Russian River is the one described as delivering demonstrated water supply and environmental flow benefit while maintaining or increasing flood risk management.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - authoritative scope of the real deployed programme
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Russian River programme page also verified 200: https://cw3e.ucsd.edu/firo_russian_river
confirmed_sources.caveat: I fetched and read it: it references 'decision support tools' and 'forecast verification methods' but publishes NO repository links, no PDF links to individual assessments, and no technical implementation detail. Contact given is kvm@ucsd.edu. Do not expect official FIRO source code to exist.

confirmed_sources.name: pywr/pywr (GitHub)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Generalised network resource-allocation model in Python/Cython. VERIFIED to include HydropowerRecorder, HydropowerTargetParameter, ControlCurveParameter, ControlCurveInterpolatedParameter and Scenario.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the ControlCurve (rule curve) and Scenario (ensemble) abstractions are exactly the two concepts AquaSync is missing, even though the framework itself is a poor fit
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install pywr   (VERIFIED: 37 packages in 30 s, clean import on Python 3.12; a 20-line JSON single-reservoir + hydropower model at Idukki scale loaded in 1.38 s and solved 31 daily steps in <0.01 s). Docs https://pywr.github.io/pywr/ (200). Paper DOI 10.1016/j.envsoft.2020.104635 (200).
confirmed_sources.caveat: Linear-programme core - head-dependent hydropower is a post-hoc Recorder or iterative target parameter, not a native nonlinear constraint. GPL-3.0 is viral, which matters if AquaSync ships to KSEB. The widely-cited paper DOI 10.1016/j.envsoft.2019.104635 is WRONG and 404s; the correct one uses the 2020 segment.

confirmed_sources.name: pywr/pywr-next (Pywr 2.0, Rust)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Rust rewrite of the Pywr compute core with a Python binding layer, retaining the Parameter system from Pywr 1.x.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - not adoptable; included so the next person does not mistake activity for readiness
confirmed_sources.last_activity: 2026-08-26 (very active), but all releases pre-release: v2.0.0-beta1 2025-10-06 through v2.0.0-beta4 2026-07-09; 2.0.0b6 to PyPI 2026-08-25; 54 open issues
confirmed_sources.caveat: Repo description still reads 'An experimental repository exploring ideas for a major revision'. Created 2020-11, nearly six years old and still beta. Building on it now guarantees rework.

confirmed_sources.name: Pywr-DRB
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: A real, maintained basin-scale reservoir-operations application built on Pywr: Delaware River Basin, NYC reservoir system, transbasin diversions, minimum-flow targets and regulatory rules (1954 Supreme Court Decree Montague target).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the best worked example of encoding real institutional operating rules in an open framework, which is precisely the problem AquaSync faces with KSEB's Idukki rule curve
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Docs https://pywr-drb.github.io/Pywr-DRB/ (200). Paper: Hamilton, Amestoy & Reed (2024) EMS 181:106185, DOI 10.1016/j.envsoft.2024.106185 (200).
confirmed_sources.caveat: Only 12 stars and heavily US-regulatory-specific. Read it for the modelling patterns (how a legal flow target becomes a constraint), not to reuse code.

confirmed_sources.name: iRONS toolbox
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Python functions for reservoir simulation, forecasting and optimisation plus interactive Jupyter Notebooks (Knowledge transfer / Implementation / Case studies). Modules: res_sys_sim.py (13 KB), operating_policy.py (12.6 KB, includes op_piecewiselin_1res - piecewise-linear release vs storage fraction), download_forecast.py (Copernicus CDS seasonal forecasts), bias_correction.py, HBV_sim.py, HBV_calibration.py.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - not as a framework to adopt (AquaSync already exceeds it) but as three donor parts: the piecewise-linear policy parameterisation, CDS forecast download + bias correction, and the best teaching notebooks for explaining FIRO to KSEB
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iRONStoolbox/iRONStoolbox/master/iRONS/Software/operating_policy.py . Project site https://ironstoolbox.github.io/ (200) offers Binder. Paper DOI 10.1016/j.envsoft.2021.105188 (200).
confirmed_sources.caveat: environment.yml pins python=3.9, numpy<2.0, pandas<2.0, matplotlib<3.5 - will not install into a modern env unrelaxed. Scope is comparable to AquaSync's ~600 lines and less calibrated (generic HBV, no tide, no Muskingum, no hill diagram). Depends on platypus-opt for optimisation.

confirmed_sources.name: pymoo
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: NSGA-II, NSGA-III, R-NSGA-III, MOEA/D, GA, DE, CMA-ES, PSO with a clean Problem/Algorithm API, reference directions and decomposition methods. Deps: numpy, scipy, moocore, autograd, cma, matplotlib, alive_progress, Deprecated.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the correct MOEA choice IF AquaSync raises policy dimensionality past ~6 variables; I benchmarked it and it buys nothing at the current 3
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install pymoo   (VERIFIED: pymoo + platypus-opt together in 1 min 13 s. NSGA-II ran 4,800 evaluations of an AquaSync-shaped 3-objective policy sim in 2.31 s vs 2.02 s for the equivalent exhaustive grid). Docs https://pymoo.org/ and https://pymoo.org/algorithms/moo/nsga2.html both 200.
confirmed_sources.caveat: Apache-2.0 makes it the only MOEA here with no licensing friction. But at 3 decision variables it is strictly worse than the grid AquaSync already runs - stochastic, approximate, and needing seed management before a front is defensible.

confirmed_sources.name: Platypus (Project-Platypus)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Python multi-objective optimisation library (NSGA-II, epsilon-NSGA-II and others). The substrate PyBorg is built on, and the optional dependency for Pywr's [opt] extra and for iRONS.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - pymoo is the better default; listed because Pywr and iRONS both reference it
confirmed_sources.last_activity: repo pushed 2026-08-03 but last PyPI release is 1.4.1 from 2024-10-07 - roughly 22 months of unreleased commits
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install platypus-opt. Docs https://platypus.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ (200).
confirmed_sources.caveat: GPL-3.0 is viral. The 22-month release gap means pip users run materially older code than the repo. Only 3 open issues.

confirmed_sources.name: DEAP
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Distributed Evolutionary Algorithms in Python - low-level EC toolkit (toolbox, operators, statistics, multiprocessing). Deps are just numpy and moocore.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - too low-level for this job; relevant only because HydroCNHS uses it for calibration
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install deap. Docs https://deap.readthedocs.io/en/master/ (200).
confirmed_sources.caveat: Most-starred tool in this dimension but the least suited - you build the MOO machinery yourself. Skip in favour of pymoo.

confirmed_sources.name: MOEA Framework
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Java framework for multi-objective optimisation with 80+ test problems and, more importantly, algorithm DIAGNOSTICS - runtime metrics, hypervolume, generational distance, attainment surfaces.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - only worth it if you must defend an MOEA's convergence quantitatively; adds a JVM dependency
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Project site https://moeaframework.org (200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Java. The Reed group uses it purely for post-processing MOEA runtime dynamics (see their MM Borg Training posts), not as a modelling tool.

confirmed_sources.name: Borg MOEA project site
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Auto-adaptive multi-operator search, dynamic population sizing, epsilon-dominance archiving. ANSI C, runs on Unix/Linux/Windows/Mac. The de-facto standard MOEA in the water-resources literature.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high as a WARNING - it underpins WaterPaths, PySedSim optimisation and most EMODPS reservoir studies, so knowing it is not open source explains why that whole family is unadoptable
confirmed_sources.license: NOT open source - site text verbatim: 'Borg is freely available for academic and non-commercial use... request access to its source code'
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Access request form (verified 200): https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfuBBDJyEVw6D8PLvwx9hmOqpmw7MCyjpeOMVbxGXzxZkG2wg/viewform - email with private BitBucket link within ~3 business days
confirmed_sources.caveat: The non-commercial clause is a genuine legal blocker if AquaSync is ever delivered as an operational product to KSEB/KSDMA. PyBorg inherits it. Community wrapper jackjackk/borg4platypus is 1 star, GPL-3.0, dead since 2019-02.

confirmed_sources.name: SDDP.jl
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Multistage stochastic dual dynamic programming as a JuMP extension - policy graphs, Markovian and stagewise-independent uncertainty, risk measures (AV@R), and simulation of trained policies.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the mature tool for the SEASONAL foresight problem (target storage entering the monsoon recession) that the event-horizon FIRO MPC does not address
confirmed_sources.license: NOASSERTION per GitHub API (MPL-2.0 in practice - verify before shipping)
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Julia: `] add SDDP`. Docs https://sddp.dev/stable/ (200). Paper DOI 10.1287/ijoc.2020.0987 (INFORMS J. Computing 2021).
confirmed_sources.caveat: Introduces a Julia runtime alongside Python. Requires a convex, stagewise-independent problem statement, so the reservoir must be linear or piecewise-linear. The doi.org link returns 403 to curl (INFORMS blocks it) though the DOI is correct.

confirmed_sources.name: do-mpc
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: General nonlinear MPC and moving-horizon estimation toolbox on CasADi/IPOPT, including robust multi-stage NMPC.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low today, medium later - overkill for a linear reservoir balance, but the natural upgrade if you later want the head-dependent turbine curve as a nonlinear constraint INSIDE the MPC
confirmed_sources.last_activity: 2025-10-31 (~10 months stale); 5.1.1 on PyPI same date; 94 open issues
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install do-mpc  (deps: casadi>=3.6.0, scipy, numpy, matplotlib, pandas; [full] adds onnx, torch>2.0.0, asyncua). Docs https://www.do-mpc.com/ (200).
confirmed_sources.caveat: Not water-specific. For AquaSync's linear mass balance with box + ramp constraints, the 40-line cvxpy formulation I verified (8.8 ms/solve) is roughly a tenth of the machinery.

confirmed_sources.name: HydroCNHS
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Semi-distributed hydrological model for coupled natural-human systems with Dam, RiverDiv, Conveying and InSitu agent APIs, plus a DEAP-based parallel calibration and uncertainty harness. Hydrology options: GWLF, ABCD, HYMOD.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - the agent-based coupling solves a problem AquaSync does not have, and its hydrology suits temperate US basins rather than a monsoon Western Ghats catchment
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install hydrocnhs (deps: deap, joblib, matplotlib, numpy, pandas, pyyaml, ruamel-yaml, scikit-learn, scipy, tqdm). LIVE docs: https://cylin928.github.io/HydroCNHS/ (200).
confirmed_sources.caveat: IMPORTANT: the repo moved from philip928lin to cylin928 and the widely-cited docs URL https://philip928lin.github.io/HydroCNHS/ now returns 404. Paper DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)WR.1943-5452.0001630 returns 403 to curl (ASCE blocks automated clients).

confirmed_sources.name: WaterPaths
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: C++ stochastic simulation of multi-utility water supply portfolios with dynamic risk-of-failure triggers for infrastructure investment pathways under deep uncertainty.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - wrong problem (multi-decade investment planning, not release scheduling) and effectively abandoned
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Paper: Trindade et al. (2020) EMS, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2020.104772 (200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Optimisation mode requires recompiling against Borg (non-commercial licence) plus mpirun. The reedgroup.github.io/Training/WaterPaths_Training.html tutorial link circulating online is DEAD (404).

confirmed_sources.name: PySedSim
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Daily-timestep river basin simulation of flow, sediment and hydropower for evaluating dam siting, design and sediment-management operations, with MOEA coupling for operating-policy discovery.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - sediment-focused, dead, and AquaSync has no sediment objective
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Paper: Wild et al. (2021) EMS, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2020.104947 (200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Python 2 / early-Python-3 era. Not on PyPI. The immm-sfa.github.io/pysedsim docs URL is DEAD (404). Listed as a verified negative.

confirmed_sources.name: M3O - Multi-Objective Optimal Operations
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: MATLAB toolbox implementing, side by side, deterministic DP, stochastic DP, implicit stochastic optimisation, sampling SDP, fitted Q-iteration, EMODPS (evolutionary multi-objective direct policy search with RBF policies) and MPC for multipurpose reservoirs.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium as a READING reference - the canonical algorithm menu for exactly this problem class; zero value as runnable code
confirmed_sources.caveat: MATLAB (commercial-licence blocker). The CIS Lab Python port Critical-Infrastructure-Systems-Lab/M3Opy is an EMPTY stub with 0 stars and no description. Every published EMODPS implementation additionally depends on the gated Borg MOEA.

confirmed_sources.name: Critical Infrastructure Systems Lab - InfeRes
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Python package that infers reservoir water extent, level and storage volume from satellite imagery.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high but for a DIFFERENT gap - the credible route to AquaSync's missing pre-2020 Idukki/Idamalayar operational record, which no operational dataset provides
confirmed_sources.caveat: Flagged because it surfaced during this search; it belongs to the data dimension, not optimisation. Remote-sensing-derived levels carry their own error budget and will not approach a 0.30 m replay MAE.

confirmed_sources.name: Critical Infrastructure Systems Lab - VICResOpt
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Optimisation of reservoir rule curves and operating rules embedded inside the VIC hydrologic model, with an NSGA-II driver. Companion to VICRes (verified 200, 27 stars, pushed 2026-03-15), which adds reservoir storage and operations to VIC.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low-medium - the only maintained-adjacent example of rule-curve optimisation coupled to a distributed hydrologic model, but it commits you to the VIC ecosystem (C, gridded, computationally heavy)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Adopting it means adopting VIC, a far heavier hydrologic engine than AquaSync's SCS-CN, which would not improve a basin already replayed to 0.30 m MAE. Applied to the Mekong, not India.

confirmed_sources.name: Inflow-Prediction-Bhakra
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: LSTM inflow forecasting and a bidirectional storage-capacity/elevation calculator for Bhakra reservoir, Satluj basin, Northern India.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - the closest thing to Indian reservoir-operation code that exists on GitHub, which is itself the finding
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.04255
confirmed_sources.caveat: Dead since 2021, single-reservoir, forecasting only (no operation optimisation). Reported to substantiate the verified negative that no Indian institutional open-source reservoir-operation package exists. The only other Indian-adjacent repo found, behzadasd/Reservoir-Operation-Optimization (200, 20 stars), is MATLAB and dead since 2019-12.

confirmed_sources.name: Reed Group software index (Cornell)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Authoritative curated index of the water-resources MOEA ecosystem: Borg MOEA, MOEA Framework, OpenMORDM, Hymod & HBV, Project Platypus, PySedSim, SALib, WaterPaths, Pywr-DRB, statemodify.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the fastest way to see the whole Reed/Cornell ecosystem and confirm nothing was missed
confirmed_sources.last_activity: actively curated; lists Pywr-DRB and statemodify (2024)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Marks everything 'Active' including WaterPaths (last push 2022-01) and PySedSim (2020-07), so its status labels are NOT reliable - verify each repo's pushed_at yourself, as I did.

confirmed_sources.name: Water Programming blog (Reed group)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Long-running practitioner blog on MOEA diagnostics, Borg/PyBorg setup, MOEA Framework post-processing, many-objective reservoir optimisation and HydroCNHS walkthroughs. The practical how-to layer the papers omit.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the PyBorg setup post is where the licensing gate is spelled out plainly, and the MOEA diagnostics posts are the standard reference for defending a Pareto front
confirmed_sources.download_hint: PyBorg setup post: https://waterprogramming.wordpress.com/2021/08/13/introduction-to-pyborg-basic-setup-and-running/ (200). Lab manual mirror: https://reedgroup.github.io/Software/BorgMOEA.html (200).

confirmed_sources.name: baobabsoluciones/flowing-basin
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Intraday multi-reservoir hydropower economic optimisation comparing RL against MILP and heuristic baselines - code behind 'Deep Reinforcement Learning for Intraday Multireservoir Hydropower Management'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - the single most substantial RL-for-reservoirs repo I could find, and it has 5 stars, which IS the finding about RL maturity in this field
confirmed_sources.caveat: 5 stars, 1 fork, no repo description. Reported to substantiate the verified negative that RL for reservoir operation has no production-grade open implementation - do not plan AquaSync work around RL. Fill-and-Spill (arXiv 2403.04195, verified 200) publishes no repository at all.

verification_notes: This domain has NOT been through the adversarial verification pass. URLs carry the researching agent's own reported status only. Treat as provisional.

dead end: Borg MOEA source code cannot be obtained by download at all. borgmoea.org gates it behind a Google form ('request access to its source code', ~3 business days, private BitBucket) and licenses it for 'academic and non-commercial use' only. This transitively poisons WaterPaths (needs a Borg recompile for optimisation mode), PySedSim's optimisation path, PyBorg, and essentially every published EMODPS reservoir study. Do not plan any AquaSync deliverable around it.

dead end: Reinforcement learning for reservoir operation - four separate GitHub searches produced nothing usable. The query 'reservoir+operation+DDPG' returned ZERO repositories. Best results anywhere: wlross/HydroPower (4 stars, dead 2020-06), Fraktal-Norge-AS/HydroRL (2 stars, 2023), vaishsRP/ReinforcementLearning-HydroelectricDam (2 stars), nanu1605/reservoir-rl (0 stars), Sarmadzandi multi-agent (4 stars, 2024). The most substantial, baobabsoluciones/flowing-basin, has 5 stars. The Fill-and-Spill paper (arXiv 2403.04195, JWRPM 150(7)) publishes no repository link. There is no reservoir-RL equivalent of stable-baselines3 - papers vastly outnumber code.

dead end: WaterPaths - do not invest. Last push 2022-01-04 (4.5 years stale), 23 stars, C++, no licence file, and it solves multi-decade multi-utility water-supply INVESTMENT pathways under deep uncertainty rather than release scheduling. Optimisation mode additionally requires recompiling against Borg plus an MPI toolchain. Its widely-linked training page (reedgroup.github.io/Training/WaterPaths_Training.html) is also dead (404).

dead end: PySedSim - dead since 2020-07-22, Python 2 era, not on PyPI, and sediment/dam-siting focused. AquaSync has no sediment objective. Its docs site (immm-sfa.github.io/pysedsim) 404s. Not worth an afternoon.

dead end: M3O - MATLAB, GPL-2.0, dead since 2019. Its CIS Lab Python port, Critical-Infrastructure-Systems-Lab/M3Opy, is an EMPTY stub: 0 stars, no description, no language detected. Read M3O for the algorithm menu; do not attempt to run or port it.

dead end: Indian institutional reservoir-operation software does not exist as open source. Four search angles (IIT/NIH Roorkee tools, India-WRIS, CWC decision-support systems, named Indian reservoirs) found no NIH Roorkee or IIT hydrological package on GitHub - github.com/IIT-Roorkee and the other IIT Roorkee orgs are student robotics/CS/vision groups. India-WRIS and CWC publish data portals and PDFs, not code. The only Indian reservoir repos are one-off paper artefacts: Anurag14/Inflow-Prediction-Bhakra (17 stars, dead 2021-09) and behzadasd/Reservoir-Operation-Optimization (20 stars, MATLAB, dead 2019-12).

dead end: The FIRO programme itself publishes no software. I fetched cw3e.ucsd.edu/firo/ directly: it lists six programmes and mentions 'decision support tools' and 'forecast verification methods' but contains ZERO repository links and no technical implementation detail (contact given is kvm@ucsd.edu). Do not go looking for an official FIRO codebase - all reusable code is academic (Herman group at UC Davis, Brodeur at NCSU).

dead end: pywr-next / Pywr 2.0 - still explicitly experimental after nearly six years (repo created 2020-11). All four GitHub releases are pre-release betas and the description still warns it is exploratory. 12 stars, 54 open issues. Building on it now guarantees rework.

dead end: swmm_mpc - dead since 2019-09 and SWMM/EPA stormwater-specific (urban drainage, pumps and orifices), not reservoir operation. It surfaces in every 'MPC water' search but does not transfer. HEC-ResSim is likewise a dead end for reuse: closed-source, Java/Windows, and its own documentation states it has no optimisation framework (v4.1 released April 2026).

dead end: Several authoritative pages block automated verification and should not be cited as links: hec.usace.army.mil (HEC-ResSim) returns curl status 000 - connection refused to non-browser clients; escholarship.org, ascelibrary.org, sciencedirect.com, agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com, iwaponline.com, mdpi.com and zenodo.org all return 403 to curl. Cite the DOI or a publisher-independent copy instead. Note doi.org itself returns 403 for ASCE (10.1061/...), INFORMS (10.1287/...) and MDPI (10.3390/...) prefixes while Elsevier DOIs (10.1016/...) resolve 200 - so a 403 on doi.org is not evidence the DOI is wrong.

dimensions.dimension: Open-source river routing, hydraulics and 2D flood inundation (plus the DEM / hydrography / gauge-data supply chain needed to drive them) for the Periyar basin

confirmed_sources.name: CWC River Water Level (Manual - Hourly) - basin 031 West flowing rivers Tadri to Kanyakumari
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Hourly manual river stage AND reservoir level CSVs. Basin-031 file 1991-2020 = 260 MB / 1,284,651 rows; 2021-2025 = 234 MB / 1,139,984 rows. Columns: Station, River, Basin, Latitude, Longitude, Is_DischargeDataAvailable, RL_of_zeroGauge, Data Acquisition Time, River Water Level Manual Hourly (meter). Periyar stations present: NEELEESWARAM (31,172 + 25,643 rows), ARANGALI (30,186 + 27,460), VANDIPERIYAR (48,949 + 26,714), Idukki (Eb)/Idukki Arch Reservoir (3,532 + 9,477), Idamalayar Reservoir (3,621 + 9,561).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - this single dataset closes the Muskingum-calibration gap (two synchronous hourly Periyar gauges), supplies a genuine hourly Aug-2018 flood hydrograph, and gives independent Idukki/Idamalayar levels back to 2019-06-10 that pre-date and can repair the corrupt amith-vp window
confirmed_sources.license: Other (Open) per CKAN license_id 'other-open'; publisher CWC / National Water Informatics Centre
confirmed_sources.last_activity: records run to 2025-12-31; a 2026-2030 resource already exists
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -L -o wl031.csv 'https://nwdp.nwic.gov.in/dataset/d951a09c-6cf8-470e-be77-e80116f13d34/resource/c94d9352-442c-4e99-ade4-537eebc251f4/download/rwl_manual_hr_cwc_031_1991_2020.csv' and .../a9f5d910-e360-42e0-a45c-637310b009c4/download/rwl_manual_hr_cwc_031_2021_2025.csv -- enumerate all 62 basin resources via https://nwdp.nwic.gov.in/api/3/action/package_show?id=river-water-level-manual-hourly-cwc-subernarekha (that odd slug is the whole CWC manual-hourly package)
confirmed_sources.caveat: No login, but you MUST find it by basin code 031, not by state - searching 'Kerala' misses it entirely. Cadence is nominally hourly at river gauges but roughly 3-hourly at the reservoirs. Some rows are mislabelled across stations (Idamalayar max 704.79 m, Idukki min 2.79 m), so range-filter before use. Reservoir series start 2019-06-10 - there is NO 2018 reservoir level here.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC River Discharge (Manual - Daily) - Kerala
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Daily gauged discharge, 52 state resources. Kerala 2001-2025 file = 39.4 MB, 217,538 rows, 40 stations. Three on the Periyar: NEELEESWARAM 8,478 values 2001-01-01..2025-12-31; ARANGALI 7,518 values; VANDIPERIYAR 14,837 values (twice-daily). A separate Kerala 1950-2000 resource also exists (verified 200).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the discharge half of the rating curve AquaSync needs to turn hourly Periyar stage into hourly Q, and an immediate independent validation series for the October 2021 case study
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -L -o kerala_q.csv 'https://nwdp.nwic.gov.in/dataset/08fa3fd0-7861-471d-a295-27c1b239d1fa/resource/c3cbe74d-2442-4496-aab2-21e8b5faa12e/download/river_discharge_manual_daily_cwc_kl_2001_2025.csv'
confirmed_sources.caveat: Manual observer record: roughly one missing day per week year-round, and a 7-day hole 2018-08-16..2018-08-22 straight across the flood peak. Record max is 6,323.5 m3/s (2013-08-05), so the CWC report's 8,800 cumec 2018 peak is NOT in this file.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC Study Report: Kerala Floods of August 2018 (Hydrology (S) Dte)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 5.7 MB PDF, Sept 2018. Section 4.1 is a Periyar-specific water balance: catchment areas (Neeleeswaram 4,033 km2, Mullaperiyar 637, Idukki free 605, Idamalayar 472), 15-17 Aug rainfall/runoff table, Idukki hourly operation narrative (731.82 m at 10 Aug 00:00; pre-release to 750 cumec spill; peak inflow 2,532 cumec at 22:00 on 15 Aug attenuated to 1,500 cumec spill = 41%; FRL 732.43 m reached 01:00 on 17 Aug), Idamalayar narrative (168.06 m on 8 Aug, peak inflow 1,164 cumec on 16 Aug, average spill 1,271 cumec, no attenuation), and Fig.3 Neeleeswaram hourly hydrograph peaking ~8,800 cumec at 14:00 on 16 Aug.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the single most quotable ground-truth document for a 2018 replay scenario, and it is hosted on the KSDMA domain, which is also a soft opening for the agency-integration gap
confirmed_sources.license: Government of India report, freely hosted by KSDMA; no explicit open licence stated
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -L -o cwc.pdf '<url>' then pdftotext -layout cwc.pdf cwc.txt (I extracted 1,766 lines to scratchpad\cwc.txt)
confirmed_sources.caveat: The hourly Idukki/Idamalayar/Neeleeswaram series exist only as chart images (Figs 3, 4, 5) - the axis labels survive pdftotext but the data values do not. You would have to digitise the figures, OR just use the NWDP hourly stage file instead, which is the real record.

confirmed_sources.name: NOAA-OWP/t-route
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Tree-based hydrologic/hydraulic routing: Muskingum-Cunge (per-segment, parallel) and Diffusive Wave (per-subnetwork, serial), Python orchestration over Fortran kernels, CLI and BMI interfaces.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the reference operational Muskingum-Cunge implementation, but it duplicates capability AquaSync already has and is expensive to point at a non-US network
confirmed_sources.last_activity: pushed_at 2026-08-18, but last commit on master is 2025-01-30 and last release v2.4.0 is 2024-10-02; all 2026 work is in open NGWPC PRs #882/#883
confirmed_sources.download_hint: git clone --branch master https://github.com/NOAA-OWP/t-route.git && ./compiler.sh (needs gfortran + NetCDF-Fortran 4.6.1, plus numpy pandas xarray netcdf4 joblib toolz pyyaml 'Cython>3,!=3.0.4' geopandas pyarrow deprecated wheel)
confirmed_sources.caveat: SETUP COST: HIGH. No native Windows - README directs Windows users to install WSL2 with Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 first. Fortran toolchain + NetCDF-Fortran build is the main pain. README states the code is still 'bespoke for NWM' and expects NHDPlus-HR or HY_Features; generalisation to arbitrary networks is described as in progress, not done. Budget 1-2 weeks to a Periyar example. 168 open issues.

confirmed_sources.name: rileyhales/river-route
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Pure-Python vectorised Muskingum-family routing (Muskingum, RapidMuskingum, UnitMuskingum) on vector stream networks using numba kernels and scipy sparse matrices. Params file is a parquet with exactly river_id, downstream_river_id, k, x, topologically sorted, outlets = -1.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - cheapest possible sanity check on AquaSync's own Muskingum implementation and its sub-reaching logic; a half-day read, not a dependency
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install river-route (requires Python >=3.12; pulls dask geopandas netcdf4 networkx numba numpy pandas pyarrow pyyaml scipy shapely tqdm xarray). Docs at https://river-route.code.hales.app/
confirmed_sources.caveat: NO calibration module - I checked the docs and the file-schema page; K and x are inputs you must supply from elsewhere. Only 4 stars, effectively a one-person project. The docs URL advertised on PyPI/GitHub (river-route.hales.app) does not resolve (curl 000); the working one is river-route.code.hales.app.

confirmed_sources.name: mhpi/dMC-Juniata-hydroDL2 (differentiable Muskingum-Cunge)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: PyTorch + Hydra implementation of Bindas et al. 2024 WRR: Muskingum-Cunge with an embedded NN mapping reach attributes (catchment area, sinuosity, slope) to Manning's n and channel geometry, trained only on downstream hydrographs.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low as code, high as a method to copy - learning K and x from reach attributes is exactly right for an ungauged Periyar reach network, but this repo will not run on your basin without a rewrite
confirmed_sources.last_activity: last push 2024-04-14; 19 commits total, zero open issues or PRs
confirmed_sources.download_hint: conda env create -f environment.yml; python -m dMC -- and separately download the Susquehanna river-graph from Zenodo record 10183429
confirmed_sources.caveat: RESEARCH-ONLY, paper replication. Hard-wired to the Susquehanna/Juniata; no bundled data; no packaging as a library; abandoned for 2+ years. The maintained successor is DeepGroundwater/ddr (Apache-2.0, 11 stars, pushed 2026-08-19, https://github.com/DeepGroundwater/ddr, verified 200).

confirmed_sources.name: delta-HBV2 / delta-MC2 global streamflow, 2.94M rivers 1980-2020
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Nature Communications 2025 paper behind the global differentiable HBV + differentiable Muskingum-Cunge run. Companion dataset on Zenodo record 20684429 (v5, 2026-06-18): 130.9 GB in 8 continent zips, discharge for 2.94M MERIT flowline reaches, 1980-2020, partitioned by MERIT-Basins pfaf zone (South India = pfaf 4).
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium-high - a plausible model-based 2018 (and 1980-2020) discharge series for Periyar reaches where no gauge exists, and the strongest published evidence that NN-learned Muskingum-Cunge parameters generalise
confirmed_sources.license: Penn State Non-Commercial Software License Agreement on the dataset - commercial use requires written PSU consent
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Asia zip from https://zenodo.org/records/20684429 (browser or WebFetch; curl from an Indian IP hits Zenodo's 403 traffic guard)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Zenodo returned 403 to curl from this network (anti-abuse throttle, not a dead link) - it resolves fine in a browser. Discharge only: the learned Manning-n and channel-geometry parameters are NOT published, so you cannot lift K and x straight out of it. And it is a model reanalysis, not observation - do not validate against it.

confirmed_sources.name: Deltares/SFINCS (+ hydromt_sfincs)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Reduced-complexity 2D compound-flood solver (SFINCS-LIE drops advection; SFINCS-SSWE keeps it). Handles fluvial + pluvial + tidal + wind/wave in one run with subgrid bathymetry, and accepts discharge point sources, water-level/tide boundaries and rainfall - exactly AquaSync's three forcings. Companion builder hydromt_sfincs (https://github.com/Deltares/hydromt_sfincs, 200, GPL-3.0, 35 stars, pushed 2026-08-18, PyPI hydromt-sfincs 1.2.2 on 2025-12-02) generates the whole schematisation from one YAML data catalogue plus an INI.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the recommended path to close the 2D-inundation gap for Aluva and the Kochi backwaters; the only 2D code here that natively couples a river discharge boundary to a tidal boundary, which is the actual physics at Aluva
confirmed_sources.license: GPL-3.0 for source; precompiled executables under Deltares Freeware (commercial + research use allowed, no redistribution/modification)
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Windows exe: https://download.deltares.nl/sfincs (200). Linux/Mac/HPC: docker pull deltares/sfincs-cpu (https://hub.docker.com/r/deltares/sfincs-cpu, 200). No Fortran build needed either way. pip install hydromt-sfincs for the builder.
confirmed_sources.caveat: The release tags carry no GitHub assets - binaries come from download.deltares.nl or Docker Hub, so pin your version manually. Docs give no quantitative speedup figures; the framing paper is Eilander et al., NHESS 23, 823, 2023 (https://nhess.copernicus.org/articles/23/823/2023/, 200). HydroMT's shipped data catalogues are Europe/US-centric - you will write Kerala entries yourself.

confirmed_sources.name: LISFLOOD-FP 8.x (SEAMLESS-WAVE / Sheffield)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The canonical academic 2D floodplain code. 8.0 added DG2/FV1 solvers; 8.1 added GPU-accelerated uniform and non-uniform ACC solvers; 8.2 (GMD 18, 9827, 2025) added GPU multiwavelet DG with dynamic resolution adaptivity and a DG2-RANS solver. Cross-platform, CMake >= 3.13.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - defensible and well-published, but it buys AquaSync accuracy it cannot yet justify at a setup cost it cannot yet afford
confirmed_sources.license: MUDDLED - the project page says 'GNU GPL v3.0 for any non-commercial use', the 8.0 Zenodo record (4073011, 2020-10-09) says 'GNU General Public License v2.0 only', and the 8.2 paper says GPL v3.0. Get this in writing before any commercial or KSEB deployment.
confirmed_sources.last_activity: 8.2 paper published 2025 in GMD (https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/18/9827/2025/, 200); 8.1 paper GMD 16, 2391, 2023 (200)
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Source zip via the Zenodo link on https://www.seamlesswave.com/Zenodo.html (200) - LISFLOOD-FP-8.zip, 53.0 MB, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.4073011. GPU 8.2 code at https://github.com/al0vya/gpu-mwdg2 (200, Cuda, 7 stars, last push 2024-05-19, NO LICENCE FILE).
confirmed_sources.caveat: SETUP COST: HIGH. CMake + C++/CUDA build, and the 8.2 benchmarks ran on an NVIDIA A100 80 GB - the reported 1.1x-4.5x adaptivity speedups are relative to their own uniform GPU solver, not to CPU. Plus roughly a week of DEM burning/conditioning before a single run. The repo carrying the 8.2 kernels has no licence file at all.

confirmed_sources.name: jsosa/LFPtools
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Python CLI suite to prepare LISFLOOD-FP inputs from global data: lfp-getdepths (three methods incl. hydraulic geometry and simplified Manning), lfp-getwidths, lfp-getbankelevs, lfp-fixelevs, lfp-prepdata. Paper reports a 1 km Severn model built in 1.45 minutes.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low-medium - the standard MERIT-Hydro-to-LISFLOOD bridge, and its bank-elevation and depth heuristics are worth reading even if you go the SFINCS route
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install git+https://github.com/jsosa/LFPtools.git (a Dockerfile is in docker/)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Effectively abandoned; expect Python-2-era and GDAL-version friction. Use the Docker image, not a fresh pip install. A LISFLOOD-FP 5.9 BMI wrapper also exists (openearth/lisflood-fp-bmi, GPL-3.0, 47 stars) but was last pushed 2021-04-12.

confirmed_sources.name: gpt-cmdr/ras-commander
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Python API for HEC-RAS 6.x: parallel plan execution, project/plan/geometry manipulation, and - crucially - standalone HDF result reading. HdfResultsMesh exposes 2D mesh depths, velocities and WSE, with export_max_depth_raster() writing a COG.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the standalone HDF reader means AquaSync could consume someone else's calibrated Periyar HEC-RAS 2D model without running HEC-RAS at all
confirmed_sources.last_activity: pushed 2026-08-25; PyPI 0.99.1 released 2026-07-21 - the most actively maintained tool in this whole dimension
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install ras-commander[all] (Python >=3.10; pulls h5py numpy pandas requests geopandas shapely; pywin32 on Windows). Docs at https://rascommander.info/ (200).
confirmed_sources.caveat: RUNNING simulations needs a real HEC-RAS install on Windows - Linux is not supported for execution. Declared version support is 3.1, 4.1, 5.0.x, 6.0, 6.3, 6.6, with HDF features targeting 6.2+; HEC-RAS 7.0.1 (reportedly 2026-06-02) is newer than that list, so verify 7.x HDF compatibility before relying on it.

confirmed_sources.name: psu-efd/pyHMT2D
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Control and semi-automation of 2D hydraulic models plus pre/post-processing. Supports SRH-2D, HEC-RAS and Backwater-1D; ras-commander credits it as the origin of its 2D data handling.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the multi-model option if you ever need SRH-2D as well, and the more academically cited of the two HEC-RAS Python layers
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install pyHMT2D
confirmed_sources.caveat: Same fundamental constraint as ras-commander: it drives HEC-RAS/SRH-2D, it does not replace them, so you still need the Windows binaries.

confirmed_sources.name: HEC-RAS (USACE) downloads
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Free 1D/2D hydraulic modelling suite. Reported current release 7.0.1 (2026-06-02, ~171 MB setup, bug-fix over 7.0); a HEC-RAS 2025 Beta 0.1.0.2965 patch reportedly issued 2026-04-17. Windows 10/11 64-bit only.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the model KSEB/KSDMA consultants and the published Periyar literature actually use, so it matters for credibility and interoperability even if AquaSync never runs it
confirmed_sources.http_status: 000 (connection refused / unreachable from this Indian network; DNS resolves to 155.83.205.15 but both HTTPS and HTTP fail, and WebFetch got ECONNREFUSED)
confirmed_sources.license: US public domain, free of charge
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Likely needs a VPN or non-Indian egress. hec.usace.army.mil was unreachable in every attempt from here.
confirmed_sources.caveat: DO NOT report this URL as live without re-testing from the deployment network - I could not reach the host at all. The version numbers above come from search-result snippets of hec.usace.army.mil pages, NOT from a page I fetched, so treat 7.0.1/2026-06-02 as unconfirmed. Windows-only; no Linux/server automation path.

confirmed_sources.name: Deltares/pyflwdir
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Pure-Python numba-accelerated terrain analysis: flow direction from elevation, upstream accumulation, Strahler/classic stream order, basin and Pfafstetter subbasin delineation, flow-direction upscaling, stream vectorisation, hydrologic elevation adjustment, and - confirmed on the docs landing page - height above nearest drainage (HAND) and geomorphic floodplain delineation.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the cheapest credible half-step toward 2D. HAND + a stage-discharge relation turns AquaSync's existing Periyar discharge into a flood-extent raster in hours, with no solver, no mesh and no CFL condition
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install pyflwdir; docs https://deltares.github.io/pyflwdir/latest/ (200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: HAND is a terrain index, not hydrodynamics: no momentum, no backwater, no timing - so it cannot represent the tidal backwater at Aluva that AquaSync already models better. Treat it as a fast screening layer, not the 2D answer. The docs landing page does not enumerate which flow-direction conventions (D8/LDD/NEXTXY) are supported; check the API reference.

confirmed_sources.name: Landlab (OverlandFlow component)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Python earth-surface modelling framework; the OverlandFlow component implements the de Almeida et al. (2012) local-inertial approximation of the 2D shallow water equations on a raster grid, returning depth, discharge and shear stress. Documented in GMD 10, 1645, 2017 (https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/10/1645/2017/, 200).
confirmed_sources.relevance: low-medium - a pip-installable 2D solver with no compiler, but the wrong stability profile for the Periyar's steep upper basin
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install landlab; tutorials at https://landlab.csdms.io/tutorials/ (200); component user guide at https://landlab.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/overland_flow_user_guide.html (200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: The user guide states outright that the algorithm 'is most stable in flat environments' and that 'instabilities can arise when trying to apply the algorithm to steep landscapes', with very small timesteps hurting performance. Fine for the flat Aluva-to-backwater reach, poor above Neeleeswaram. The GitHub Releases page is stale (v2.0.1, 2020) - go by PyPI.

confirmed_sources.name: ANUGA (anuga-community/anuga_core)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Finite-volume unstructured-triangle 2D shallow water solver for dam-break, riverine and tsunami inundation, in Python with C kernels.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low-medium - genuinely open and maintained, and unstructured meshes suit an estuary, but it needs mesh-generation work AquaSync has no budget for yet
confirmed_sources.license: reported as 'Other' by the GitHub licence API (not a clean SPDX identifier) - verify before commercial use
confirmed_sources.stars: 53 on the maintained anuga-community fork; 227 on the older GeoscienceAustralia/anuga_core (last push 2026-06-22)
confirmed_sources.download_hint: See readthedocs install page; conda-forge is the usual route
confirmed_sources.caveat: Two live forks with different star counts is a real governance smell - use anuga-community, not GeoscienceAustralia. Unstructured meshing is the hidden cost: budget days of mesh design for the Periyar-to-backwater domain.

confirmed_sources.name: open TELEMAC-MASCARET
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: EDF-led CFD suite; TELEMAC-2D solves depth-averaged Saint-Venant on unstructured meshes. Consortium-governed open source since 2010.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low - overkill for AquaSync's question, and the heaviest setup cost in this list
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Easiest entry is a Docker image (e.g. flussplan/docker-telemac) or the SALOME-HYDRO Debian package; a source build is Fortran + Python + MPI
confirmed_sources.caveat: SETUP COST: VERY HIGH. Fortran toolchain, MPI, and a mesh/GIS pre-processing chain (SALOME-HYDRO is Debian-only). Weeks, not days. Do not pick this over SFINCS for a decision-support tool.

confirmed_sources.name: Iber (+ IberSWMM+)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 2D depth-averaged shallow-water model with hydrodynamics, sediment transport, water quality and rainfall-runoff; a C++/OpenMP/CUDA GPU build reports up to ~200x over the sequential version for large models. IberSWMM+ couples it 2D-1D with EPA SWMM for urban pluvial flooding (J. Hydrology 2025).
confirmed_sources.relevance: low-medium - free, GUI-driven, GPU-capable, and the SWMM coupling is the natural route if Kochi street drainage ever matters (pyswmm, PyPI 2.1.0 on 2025-09-09, 381 stars, would be the Python side)
confirmed_sources.license: free of charge from iberaula.es; NOT a recognised open-source licence - source is not openly distributed
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Register/download installer at https://www.iberaula.es/space/54/downloads
confirmed_sources.caveat: 'Free' is not 'open source' - you get executables, not code, so it cannot be embedded in an AquaSync deployment the way SFINCS or LISFLOOD-FP can. Windows-oriented GUI workflow. Note iberaula.com does not resolve (curl 000); the correct domain is iberaula.es.

confirmed_sources.name: NOAA-OWP/inundation-mapping (HAND-FIM)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The operational HAND-based Flood Inundation Mapping framework: derives HAND from a DEM, builds reach-averaged synthetic rating curves, and converts a discharge forecast to an inundation raster at continental scale.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the reference implementation of the exact discharge-to-extent trick AquaSync needs, and the cheapest bridge from its existing Periyar discharge output to a map
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Docker-based workflow in the repo README; a lighter wrapper is sdmlua/FIMserv (AGPL-3.0, 30 stars, pushed 2026-08-17, https://github.com/sdmlua/FIMserv, verified 200), published as FIMserv v1.0 in Env. Model. & Software 2025
confirmed_sources.caveat: Hard-wired to US inputs: NHDPlus V21 hydrofabric, NWM reach IDs, US HUC8 tiling, USGS 3DEP DEMs. Porting to the Periyar means substituting MERIT-Basins reaches plus a Kerala DEM and rebuilding the synthetic rating curves - realistically 1-2 weeks. Reimplementing the concept on pyflwdir's HAND is probably faster than porting this.

confirmed_sources.name: FABDEM V1-2 (Forest And Buildings removed Copernicus DEM)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Global 1 arc-second (~30 m) bare-earth DEM produced by machine-learning removal of tree and building height bias from Copernicus GLO-30. Published behind Hawker et al., Environ. Res. Lett. 17, 024016 (https://dx.doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ac4d4f, verified 200). Distributed as 10x10 degree zips of 1-degree tiles.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - for floodplain hydraulics a bare-earth DEM matters more than raw resolution, and FABDEM is the best free bare-earth option over Kerala's heavily vegetated Periyar corridor
confirmed_sources.http_status: 200 (this Bristol landing page). The actual data host data.bris.ac.uk returned 000 from this network - DNS resolves to 137.222.0.78 but the connection fails in 0.67 s, so it appears blocked rather than down.
confirmed_sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 - NON-COMMERCIAL. Commercial queries go to fabdem@fathom.global
confirmed_sources.last_activity: V1-2 is the current release; V1-0 is superseded
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Tile zips live under https://data.bris.ac.uk/data/dataset/s5hqmjcdj8yo2ibzi9b4ew3sn - retest from the deployment network. A Google Earth Engine community copy exists at https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/fabdem/ (verified 200).
confirmed_sources.caveat: TWO blockers: the NC clause rules out any commercial KSEB deployment without a Fathom licence, and I could not reach data.bris.ac.uk at all from here. Verify both before committing the DEM choice.

confirmed_sources.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Global 30 m DSM with flattened water bodies, consistent river flow direction, and edited shorelines. Free and open worldwide. Mirrored on AWS Open Data (S3, no egress cost) and on OpenTopography.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the pragmatic default DEM for a first SFINCS build: openly licensed, no registration, and its hydrologically-edited water surfaces beat raw SRTM/NASADEM
confirmed_sources.license: free and open (ESA/Copernicus licence, permits commercial use) - unlike FABDEM
confirmed_sources.last_activity: 2024_1 release current on the Earth Engine catalogue
confirmed_sources.download_hint: AWS S3 per the registry page, or the OpenTopography raster UI at https://portal.opentopography.org/raster?opentopoID=OTSDEM.032021.4326.3 (verified 200). NOTE: the programmatic endpoint portal.opentopography.org/API/globaldem returned 401 to an unauthenticated call - a free API key is required.
confirmed_sources.caveat: It is a DSM, not bare earth - tree canopy and buildings are in the surface, which will over-constrain floodplain conveyance along the vegetated Periyar. Use it for the first cut, then A/B against FABDEM. NASADEM (https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/products/nasadem_hgtv001/, verified 200, open licence, Earthdata login) is strictly worse for this purpose - older radar DSM, worse vegetation bias - so do not bother re-researching it.

confirmed_sources.name: MERIT Hydro / MERIT DEM
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 90 m globally consistent hydrography built on the error-corrected MERIT DEM: flow direction, flow accumulation, river width, upstream area, upstream gradient, and HAND - explicitly designed for large-scale hydrodynamic and flood simulation. Base DEM at https://hydro.iis.u-tokyo.ac.jp/~yamadai/MERIT_DEM/ (verified 200).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the standard input to LFPtools, hydromt_sfincs and MERIT-Basins; the pre-computed river width and HAND layers save real work
confirmed_sources.last_activity: v0.7 is the version MERIT-Basins v1.0 is built on
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Complete a Google Form on the MERIT Hydro page; the download password arrives by email. Not a direct curl.
confirmed_sources.caveat: 90 m is coarse for street-level Kochi flooding - use it for network topology, reach geometry priors (width, slope) and Muskingum K estimates, and use GLO-30/FABDEM for the inundation grid. The registration gate means you cannot script the fetch.

confirmed_sources.name: MERIT-Basins (reachhydro.org)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Global vector hydrography: ~2.94M river reaches plus unit catchments, derived from MERIT-Hydro v0.7. Files named riv_pfaf_XX_MERIT_Hydro_v07_Basins_v01.shp and cat_pfaf_XX_... . Attributes include lengthkm, slope, uparea, order (Strahler), and topology fields NextDownID, maxup, up1-up4. South India/Kerala falls in Pfafstetter level-1 zone 4.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - gives AquaSync a ready-made reach network with the length and slope a geometry-based Muskingum K needs, keyed on the same COMIDs as the delta-MC2 and GRFR global datasets
confirmed_sources.last_activity: v1.0 built on MERIT-Hydro v0.7; bugfix distribution via Google Drive
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Google Drive folder linked from the page (pfaf zone 4 for South Asia); Globus mirror also offered
confirmed_sources.caveat: NC licence again - a recurring theme across the best hydrography (MERIT-Basins, GRFR and FABDEM are all NC). Channel WIDTH is not an attribute here (slope is); width comes from MERIT Hydro rasters. Cite Lin et al. 2019 WRR (doi 10.1029/2019WR025287; note agupubs returns 403 to curl - publisher bot guard, not a dead DOI).

confirmed_sources.name: GRFR - Global Reach-level Flood Reanalysis
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 3-hourly and daily river discharge for the same 2.94M MERIT-Basins reaches, 1980-2019, with extracted flood events using a 2-year return-flow threshold. Citation Yang et al. 2021 BAMS.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium-high - an immediately usable 3-hourly modelled 2018 Periyar hydrograph at reach level, which is the right temporal resolution for Muskingum work, unlike the daily gauge record
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Daily via Google Drive folder 1hBtu-wOWbY3UUal73tdpEWx3DX6nlf5i (verified 200); 3-hourly discharge and runoff via Globus endpoints listed on the page
confirmed_sources.caveat: Naturalised reanalysis - it does NOT know about Idukki, Idamalayar or Mullaperiyar operations, so it will badly misrepresent regulated Periyar flow. Use it for unregulated tributary inflows and reach travel-time priors, never as a validation target. The BAMS DOI returns 403 to curl (publisher bot guard).

confirmed_sources.name: HydroSHEDS / HydroRIVERS
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Global river network line shapefiles at 15 arc-second resolution, distributed by continent (Asia covers India), with HydroBASINS catchments and HydroATLAS attributes alongside.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the only major hydrography here with a licence permitting commercial use, which matters if AquaSync ever ships to KSEB commercially
confirmed_sources.license: free for scientific, educational AND commercial use with attribution - the cleanest licence of any hydrography in this list
confirmed_sources.last_activity: v1.1 GeoTIFF core data is current; v1.0 BIL/GRID legacy formats are declared obsolete
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Continental zips from https://www.hydrosheds.org/hydrosheds-core-downloads (200); technical doc at https://data.hydrosheds.org/file/technical-documentation/HydroRIVERS_TechDoc_v10.pdf (200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Coarser and less hydrodynamically tuned than MERIT-Basins - fine for maps and basin delineation, weaker for reach geometry. Download by continent, not country.

confirmed_sources.name: ISRO Bhoonidhi (NRSC) - CartoDEM access
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: ISRO's current EO data hub and the live route to CartoDEM (Cartosat-1 derived Indian national DEM). CartoDEM at 30 m and coarser is free; the archive documents 1/3 arc-sec source subsampled to 1 and 3 arc-sec.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the politically and institutionally right DEM for an India-deployed system, and the one KSEB/KSDMA would recognise, but not obviously better than GLO-30 for hydraulics
confirmed_sources.license: EULA acceptance required at registration; government users (ministries, PSUs, government R&D and academic institutions) get data without further clearance. Sub-30 m products are commercial via NSIL.
confirmed_sources.last_activity: Bhoonidhi brochure dated 2025; the UIM2024 CartoDSM help doc verified 200
confirmed_sources.download_hint: EXACT PROCEDURE: (1) register at bhoonidhi.nrsc.gov.in/bhoonidhi/registration.html and accept the EULA; (2) log in; (3) search by AOI; (4) free products land in the 'Direct download' half of the Open Data Cart (the other half is 'On Order'). Legacy route: Bhuvan Open Data Archive at https://bhuvan-app3.nrsc.gov.in/data/download/index.php (200) -> Satellite/Sensor -> Cartosat-1 -> CartoDEM Versions. CartoDEM readme: https://bhuvan-app3.nrsc.gov.in/data/download/tools/document/CartoDEMReadme_v1_u1_23082011.pdf (200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Registration-gated, tile-by-tile, no scriptable API - budget half a day of clicking for the Periyar corridor. CartoDEM v1 vertical accuracy over vegetated Western Ghats terrain is not well characterised in the free documentation, which dates from 2011. Also NOT bare-earth.

confirmed_sources.name: GHI / GHSA - Geospatial dataset for Hydrologic analyses in India / South Asia
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Quality-controlled CWC/WRIS gauge metadata, catchment boundaries and hydrometeorological time series. v1 (ESSD 2023): 472 vetted stations, Peninsular India, water years 1950-2020. v2 (Zenodo 13852439, 2024-09-27, ghi_v2409.zip 653.4 MB): 1,677 stations with a 48-field stations_ghi.txt, basins_ghi shapefile and per-station catchment shapefiles. GHSA (ghsa_v2504.zip, 784.3 MB): 1,702 stations across Bhutan, China, India, Nepal, Pakistan, 1950-2023.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the fastest way to get a QC'd, relocated gauge location and delineated catchment for Neeleeswaram, to sanity-check a Muskingum reach and the CWC report's 4,033 km2 catchment area
confirmed_sources.http_status: 200 (paper). Zenodo records returned 403 to curl from this IP but resolve fine via browser/WebFetch.
confirmed_sources.license: CC BY 4.0 - commercially usable, unlike most of the hydrography above
confirmed_sources.last_activity: GHSA v2504 is the current release; GHI v2 dated 2024-09-27
confirmed_sources.download_hint: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7563599 resolves to the latest version (currently GHSA). GHI v2 specifically: https://zenodo.org/records/13852439
confirmed_sources.caveat: IMPORTANT LIMITATION I verified in the readme: streamflow is distributed at ANNUAL and MONTHLY resolution only (flow_mcm_obs, flow_mcm_tot), with days_avail/days_tot as mere counters. DAILY streamflow is NOT in the package despite the paper discussing daily data. So it is a metadata/catchment resource for AquaSync, not a hydrograph source - go to NWDP for the actual series.

confirmed_sources.name: GUARDIAN - sub-daily river discharge over India
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Scientific Data 2024. Extends India-WRIS stage into sub-daily discharge at 210 gauging stations: hourly during the monsoon (June-Sept), sub-daily otherwise, 2020 onward, by fitting rating curves with four algorithms and keeping only those with NSE >= 0.6. ~800,000 discharge points per year.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high as METHOD - precisely the recipe AquaSync should run on Neeleeswaram to convert its hourly stage into hourly discharge, complete with an NSE acceptance threshold and published code
confirmed_sources.license: paper CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; data on figshare doi 10.6084/m9.figshare.27004282 (verified, resolves 202)
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Code: https://github.com/girishpatidar/discharge_india (verified 200, Jupyter Notebook, 5 stars, NO LICENCE FILE). Data: figshare DOI above.
confirmed_sources.caveat: The paper never confirms Neeleeswaram is among the 210 stations - the station list is a figure, not a parseable table. Coverage starts 2020, so it will not give you 2018. Treat this as a method to copy, not a dataset to consume. The code repo has no licence and is one person's notebooks.

confirmed_sources.name: Global Flood Database v1 (2000-2018)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 913 mapped flood events from MODIS at 250 m, each image giving maximum flood extent, inundation duration and cloud-observation quality, filterable by date, country or Dartmouth Flood Observatory ID. The August 2018 Kerala event is in the collection.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - an OBSERVED 2018 inundation extent to validate any 2D model AquaSync eventually builds, which is otherwise the hardest thing to obtain for this basin
confirmed_sources.license: open via the Earth Engine catalogue
confirmed_sources.last_activity: v1 ends 2018 - exactly the year of interest
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Earth Engine ImageCollection GLOBAL_FLOOD_DB/MODIS_EVENTS/V1, filter to the Kerala 2018 DFO event; portal at https://global-flood-database.cloudtostreet.ai/ (verified 200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: 250 m MODIS under monsoon cloud is a weak validation target - persistent cloud on 15-17 Aug 2018 means the max-extent layer is partly interpolated. Better alternatives: the PLOS One Sentinel-1/Otsu Kerala-2018 study (https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0237324, verified 200) describes a reproducible GEE workflow, and the International Charter activated for this event (https://disasterscharter.org/activations/flood-in-india-activation-582-, verified 200). NOTE: I found NO evidence of a Copernicus EMS EMSR activation for Kerala 2018 - India went via the Charter instead.

confirmed_sources.name: ec-jrc/lisflood-code (LISFLOOD-OS, the JRC hydrological model)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Spatially distributed rainfall-runoff-routing model in Python, the engine behind EFAS and GloFAS v3.1+ and the European Drought Observatory. Represents snow, interception, infiltration, groundwater, lakes, DAMS, irrigation and channel/floodplain flow.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low-medium - NAME COLLISION WARNING: this is NOT LISFLOOD-FP. It is catchment hydrology, not a 2D inundation solver. Its reservoir module is worth reading for how an operational forecasting system parameterises dam releases, which is a live AquaSync design question.
confirmed_sources.license: EUPL-1.2 - a genuine open-source licence, commercially usable
confirmed_sources.download_hint: See https://ec-jrc.github.io/lisflood-code/ (verified 200); model docs at ec-jrc.github.io/lisflood-model
confirmed_sources.caveat: Confusing the two LISFLOODs is the most common error in this literature. LISFLOOD-FP = Bristol/Sheffield 2D floodplain hydraulics. LISFLOOD-OS = JRC distributed hydrology. They share nothing but a name. JRC LISFLOOD also needs a large static-map parameter set; the GloFAS maps are at https://data.jrc.ec.europa.eu/dataset/68050d73-9c06-499c-a441-dc5053cb0c86.

verification_notes: This domain has NOT been through the adversarial verification pass. URLs carry the researching agent's own reported status only. Treat as provisional.
