dimensions.dimension: State of the art in dam operation decision support: what is deployed, what fails

confirmed_sources.name: CAG Report No. 6 of 2021 - Performance Audit: Preparedness and Response to Floods in Kerala
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The single most valuable document found. Official audit with IISc Bangalore as technical consultant. Contains: the exact 1983 and 2020 rule curves for Idukki and Idamalayar (Appendix 3.3, 10-day steps in m MSL); daily 10-Jun to 29-Sep 2018 tables of reservoir level, inflow, powerhouse discharge, evaporation and spills for both reservoirs (Appendices 3.5-3.7, 112 dates); daily observed Neeleswaram flow (Table 3.4); simulations showing the 2020 rule curve would have INCREASED Idukki spills (531.03 vs 467.51 MCM actual) while cutting Idamalayar spills 5% (323.49 vs 340.50); HEC-RAS inundation results (520.04 -> 441.44 km2 with no spills, depth 12.32 -> 9.68 m); LULC change (+450% built-up 1985-2015, -17% water bodies); and KSEB's detailed rebuttal in the government reply (combined inflow 946.40 MCM, outflow 815.37 MCM, moderation 131.03 MCM).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - closes AquaSync's no-2018-data gap, supplies the official rule curve the optimiser must respect, and is the strongest evidence complicating the project's thesis
confirmed_sources.license: Government of India audit report, public
confirmed_sources.last_activity: presented to the Kerala Legislature 11 November 2021
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A 'Mozilla/5.0' -o cag_kerala.pdf '<url>' ; extract appendix tables with PyMuPDF word coordinates (group get_text('words') by rounded y) - pdftotext -layout scrambles the columns
confirmed_sources.caveat: Appendix 3.2 (1983 rule curve) is a scanned image with no extractable text. The daily appendix tables are simulations, but the inflow / powerhouse-discharge / evaporation columns are the observed 2018 forcing. Provenance is KSEBL data via IISc, not an independent gauge.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC Study Report: Kerala Floods of August 2018 (Hydrology (S) Directorate)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Primary official 'dams did not cause it' analysis. Idukki: 731.82 m on 10 Aug (0.61 m below FRL, only ~40 MCM cushion), drawn to 730.80 m by 13 Aug (~90 MCM), peak inflow 2532 cumec at 22:00 on 15 Aug against 1614 cumec release = 41% attenuation, FRL touched 01:00 on 17 Aug, 60 MCM of a 435 MCM three-day inflow absorbed. Idamalayar: 168.06 m on 8 Aug (97% of live storage), peak inflow 1164 cumec, average spill 1271 cumec, NO attenuation. Neeleswaram peak 8800 cumec at 15:00 on 16 Aug, EL 12.4 m against a 1974 HFL of 11.105 m. Discharging capacities 5013 cumec (Idukki) / 3012 cumec (Idamalayar). Concludes even a 75%-filled reservoir could not have mitigated it, and recommends reviewing rule curves for all reservoirs above 200 MCM live storage.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the authoritative baseline hydrology for the Periyar in Aug 2018 and the origin of Kerala's 2020 rule curves
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A 'Mozilla/5.0' -o cwc_aug2018.pdf '<url>' && pdftotext -layout cwc_aug2018.pdf
confirmed_sources.caveat: CWC's Idamalayar peak inflow (1164 cumec) directly contradicts KSEBL's 2328 cumec quoted in the CAG report. Do not treat either as ground truth without reconciling them. CWC also omits Kallarkutty releases, a criticism raised in the SANDRP threads.

confirmed_sources.name: Sudheer et al. (2019), Role of dams on the floods of August 2018 in Periyar River Basin, Kerala, Current Science 116(5):780-794
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The HEC-HMS study the Kerala government relies on. Twelve scenarios of reservoir storage (85/75/50/25%) at end-June and end-July 2018. Only 16-21% peak attenuation from advance emptying; below 50% storage downstream flows become insensitive to reservoir state; bank-full ~3400 m3/s at L1 and ~4200 m3/s at Neeleswaram against an 8800 m3/s event; the virgin no-dam simulation gives 8224 and 11990 m3/s, so dams DID attenuate 33% at L1 and 17% at L2. Aug 2018 rainfall 145-year return period, Neeleswaram flood 142-year. Critically it states the probability of detection of >25 mm/day rainfall at 3-day or 5-day lead, even with a model ensemble, is only 20-30% with a large false-alarm probability.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - defines the realistic upper bound on what any reservoir-operation optimiser can achieve in this basin, and quantifies the forecast-skill ceiling
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A 'Mozilla/5.0' -o sudheer.pdf 'https://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/116/05/0780.pdf'
confirmed_sources.caveat: Methodologically attacked by J. Harsha (CWC) for SCS-CN with lambda=0.2 untested for the Periyar and 2010 land cover extrapolated to 2018. The lead author is now ex-officio Principal Secretary to the Government of Kerala, so the paper is not politically neutral.

confirmed_sources.name: Mishra et al., The Kerala flood of 2018: combined impact of extreme rainfall and reservoir storage (HESS Discussions preprint hess-2018-480)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The preprint the court-appointed Amicus Curiae relied on. Finds 6 of 7 major reservoirs above 90% capacity on 8 Aug 2018 and >500-year return-period rainfall upstream of Idukki, Kakki and Periyar. The full referee thread and author responses are public (1 referee report, 3 short comments, 5 author responses).
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - historically pivotal but must be cited with its status, never as a peer-reviewed result
confirmed_sources.last_activity: posted 14 September 2018; discussion closed without acceptance
confirmed_sources.download_hint: PDF at https://hess.copernicus.org/preprints/hess-2018-480/hess-2018-480.pdf (verified 200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: NOT PEER-REVIEWED AND NOT PUBLISHED. Copernicus status: 'The manuscript was not accepted for further review after discussion.' Any AquaSync material citing this must say so, or it repeats the exact error the Kerala government used to dismiss the Amicus Curiae report.

confirmed_sources.name: SANDRP guest article: Role of dams in Kerala floods - Distortion of Science (J. Harsha, Director, CWC Chennai)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The technical rebuttal Current Science refused to publish. Attacks Sudheer et al.'s SCS-CN parameterisation (lambda=0.2 taken from USDA and never validated for the Periyar), the use of 2010 IRS-AWiFS land cover extrapolated to 2018 (an unstated stationarity assumption), missing rule-curve and sedimentation data for the 17 PRB reservoirs, and error accumulation through HEC-HMS. The comment thread carries a detailed counter-calculation: with a 25% cushion Idukki could have absorbed 365 MCM against a 435 MCM three-day inflow, and Idamalayar 255 MCM against 199 MCM of releases.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the specific criticisms land squarely on the SCS-CN rainfall-runoff method AquaSync itself uses, in this exact basin
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L with a full Chrome UA returns 200; WebFetch gets 403 on sandrp.in. Strip HTML tags to read.
confirmed_sources.caveat: Advocacy-site publication, not peer-reviewed - because Current Science declined it without peer review. Author is a serving CWC officer writing personally. Treat as an informed technical critique, not an adjudicated finding.

confirmed_sources.name: SANDRP: Response of Sudheer et al. to J. Harsha's comments, with Harsha's rejoinder
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The other half of the exchange - the IIT Madras team's defence of their assumptions and Harsha's reply. The only place the full argument appears in one thread.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - needed to represent the disagreement fairly rather than quoting only the attack
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl with a browser UA (WebFetch returns 403)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Same provenance caveat as the Harsha critique.

confirmed_sources.name: Vegad & Mishra (2025), Climate change and effectiveness of dams in flood mitigation in India, npj Natural Hazards
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 178 major Indian dams, in-situ plus satellite observations with hydrological and hydrodynamic simulation. Dam effectiveness in flood mitigation depends MORE on antecedent reservoir storage than on upstream precipitation variability; most downstream floods occur when reservoirs exceed 90% of capacity; dams are more effective in July than in the later monsoon; days with storage above 90% are projected to rise from ~6 at 1C to 23 at 3C global warming. Concludes India needs 'more advanced approaches for dam operations integrated with early warning of extreme inflow and reservoir storage'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the strongest recent peer-reviewed support for AquaSync's premise, from the same group whose 2018 preprint was rejected, and it quantifies how climate change erodes the very cushion the optimiser exploits
confirmed_sources.last_activity: published 17 July 2025; Research Square preprint 10.21203/rs.3.rs-6258710/v1 dated 26 March 2025
confirmed_sources.download_hint: DOI 10.1038/s44304-025-00117-z. nature.com issues a 303 to idp.nature.com for automated fetch - use the Research Square preprint or api.crossref.org for the abstract.
confirmed_sources.caveat: National-scale, not Periyar-specific. Same lead-author group as the rejected 2018 preprint, so expect the Kerala government to discount it.

confirmed_sources.name: Suresh et al. (2024), Satellite-based Tracking of Reservoir Operations ... 2018 Extreme Weather Event in Kerala (Remote Sensing of Environment) - open NASA NTRS manuscript
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: RAT 3.0 applied to 19 Kerala reservoirs for 2018 with verified inflow skill: Idamalayar r=0.81 / RMSE 135.29 cumec / NRMSE 13.30%; Kakki r=0.83 / 83.54 / 11.19%; Banasurasagar r=0.78 / 31.81 / 14.14%; IDUKKI r=0.63 / 217.94 cumec / 12.45% - degraded because Mullaperiyar intercepts and re-regulates upstream flow, requiring a bespoke regulation algorithm. Mean cloud cover >40% (sometimes >80%) makes optical surface-area retrieval unusable, motivating SWOT/microwave. Cites Ryan et al. 2020 for Kakki: a week's advance drawdown from >90% capacity would have given ~50% peak outflow reduction. 9 of 19 reservoirs were at 90% of maximum surface area by 25 July 2018, 16 of 19 by 8 August.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - independent quantified evidence of how hard Idukki inflow estimation is, and the benchmark AquaSync's inflow model should be measured against
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A 'Mozilla/5.0' -o rat_kerala.pdf '<url>' && pdftotext -layout
confirmed_sources.caveat: The ScienceDirect version of record is paywalled (400/403 to automated fetch). This is the accepted manuscript, so page and figure numbers differ from the journal version.

confirmed_sources.name: Das et al. (2025), Forecast-Informed Reservoir Operations within a Satellite-Based Framework for Mountainous and High-Precipitation Regions: Case of the 2018 Kerala Floods, J. Hydrologic Engineering 30(2)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Published prior art on essentially AquaSync's thesis: forecast-informed reservoir operation applied to the 2018 Kerala flood using GEFS precipitation forecasts within the RAT satellite framework. Reported by the same group as finding GEFS has sufficient skill - if used for trends with bias adjustment - to predict reservoir inflow peaks about a week ahead, with peak timing and rate of rise matching well.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - AquaSync must position against this, not around it; it is the closest published competitor

confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Official dam-owner site covering 59 structures including the four majors (Idukki, Idamalayar, Kakki, Banasurasagar). confirmed_sources.name: Dam Safety Act 2021 (Act No. 41 of 2021) - full text
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Verified full text (459 KB, real PDF, correct gazette header). s.35(1)(a): every specified-dam owner shall establish a hydro-meteorological network AND AN INFLOW FORECASTING SYSTEM; (b) an emergency flood warning system downstream; (c) periodic testing of both; (e) make maximum anticipated inflows/outflows and adverse-impact information available to district authorities and IN THE PUBLIC DOMAIN; (f) assist the Authority's real-time hydrological and meteorological early warning exchange. s.35(2) risk assessment within five years. s.36 Emergency Action Plan within five years for existing dams, with mandatory consultation with disaster-management agencies and owners of nearby dams. s.41 imprisonment up to one year for obstruction or refusal to comply with a direction, up to two years if it causes loss of life. s.42 head of a Government Department deemed guilty.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - simultaneously the legal mandate that justifies AquaSync and the liability structure that explains why operators will not deviate from a published rule curve on a model's advice
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A 'Mozilla/5.0' -o dsa.pdf '<url>' && pdftotext -layout. National portals verified live: https://ndsa.gov.in/en/dam-safety-act-2021 (200) and https://damsafety.in/ (200).

confirmed_sources.name: Lake Mendocino FIRO Final Viability Assessment (December 2020)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The definitive FIRO reference. Table E.1 alternatives and median 10-May storage increase (baseline 0%, EFO 27%, Hybrid EFO 15%, Modified Hybrid EFO 20% preferred, Five-Day Deterministic 18%). Forecast verification: 24-hr precip R2 0.83/0.65/0.54/0.39 at 1/3/4/5-day lead; 24-hr inflow R2 0.84/0.73/0.66/0.53. Economics $9.4M/yr (EFO reach option $9.9M), positive everywhere except hydropower. Section 4 documents the WY2019 and WY2020 major deviations; Section 7.4 sets the strategy - update the WCM, request a five-year major deviation, expand the research-and-operations partnership. Explicit disclaimer that the FVA 'does not address all USACE regulations and requirements for a potential update of the Water Control Manual'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the template for the evidence burden AquaSync would face, and the source of the honest forecast-skill numbers
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A 'Mozilla/5.0' -o mendo_fva.pdf '<url>' (11.3 MB) && pdftotext -layout
confirmed_sources.caveat: The recommended citation URL escholarship.org/uc/item/3b63q04n returns 202 (a Cloudflare interstitial, not a real failure) - use this cw3e PDF. Superseded on the regulatory question by the October 2025 WCM signing.

confirmed_sources.name: Prado Dam FIRO Final Viability Assessment (December 2023)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Second completed FVA. Steering committee formed late 2017, first met March 2018, PVA 2021, FVA Dec 2023. Buffer pool raised 498 -> 505 ft in April 2021 by an interim WCM modification. 26 scenarios over a 1990-2019 hindcast plus 100/200/500-year scaled events against 12 decisional metrics. Buffer pool 508-512 ft yields 4,000-6,000 AF/yr additional groundwater recharge; 520 ft yields ~12,000 AF/yr. Recommends exploring 510-512 ft during interim operations. Two WCM updates planned: #1 for the 10,000 -> 30,000 cfs channel capacity increase, #2 to formally incorporate FIRO. A planned MINOR deviation at 508 ft is the near-term mechanism.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - shows the graduated regulatory ladder (interim WCM change -> minor deviation -> full WCM update) and that FIRO benefits there are coupled to physical works, not software alone
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A 'Mozilla/5.0' -o prado_fva.pdf '<url>' (10 MB) && pdftotext -layout
confirmed_sources.caveat: Prado's benefit is groundwater recharge, not flood control or hydropower, so the transfer to a hydropower-first basin like the Periyar is not direct. Formal FIRO adoption still awaits WCM update #2.

confirmed_sources.name: Scripps/UCSD: New forecast-informed decision-making tool implemented at Coyote Valley Dam and Lake Mendocino
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Confirms the water control manual update was signed 22 October 2025 by USACE, Sonoma Water, Scripps/CW3E and California DWR; the first redefinition of flood-control operating rules in the dam's 66-year history; authorising an additional 11,650 acre-feet into flood control space at USACE discretion when forecasts and decision support tools indicate it is safe.

confirmed_sources.download_hint: WebFetch reads it cleanly

confirmed_sources.name: USACE Draft EA: Water Year 2021-2026 Major Planned Deviation to the Coyote Valley Dam - Lake Mendocino Water Control Manual
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The NEPA document bridging the FVA and the permanent WCM. Authorises storing an additional 11,650 acre-feet above the existing guide curve for WY2021 through WY2026, evaluating Hybrid and Modified Hybrid operations plus EFO alternatives, with NMFS coordination on listed salmonids. Demonstrates the deviation figure and the eventual permanent WCM figure are identical.

confirmed_sources.name: Forbis et al. (2025), Application of forecast-informed reservoir operations at US Army Corps of Engineers dams in California, J. Flood Risk Management 18(1)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Open-access USACE-authored account. States plainly that 'implementing FIRO at any given site is accomplished through updating its WCM'. Names the barriers: forecast skill at sufficient lead time is the gating factor; stream-gauge infrastructure gaps; more than 400 WCMs exist so doing them one-by-one 'would take decades'; WCM funding continuity is unclear; not every reservoir can implement FIRO; USACE operations are 'nearly exclusively based on rule curves' so FIRO must fit inside that paradigm rather than replace it. Documents the FIRO Screening Process (steering committee 2021, beta test in South Pacific Division 2022-2024, Stage A portfolio-wide, Stage B from early 2025).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the most honest institutional account of what fails, written from inside the agency
confirmed_sources.download_hint: DOI 10.1111/jfr3.13051. curl needs full browser headers - a bare 'Mozilla/5.0' UA gets 403, a Chrome UA plus Accept headers gets 200.
confirmed_sources.caveat: US-specific; says nothing about monsoon regimes or hydropower-first systems.

confirmed_sources.name: Delaney et al. (2020), Forecast Informed Reservoir Operations Using Ensemble Streamflow Predictions for a Multipurpose Reservoir in Northern California, Water Resources Research
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The EFO algorithm itself: each member of a CNRFC ensemble streamflow prediction is routed through the reservoir individually to compute the probability of reaching critical operational thresholds, and releases are set to keep forecast risk under a risk tolerance curve pre-trained on historical event forecasts. With an optimised risk tolerance curve EFO gives a 33% increase in median end-of-flood-season (10 May) storage without marked change in downstream flood frequency. 114 citations.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the concrete deployed answer to AquaSync's perfect-foresight problem: replace foresight with an explicit risk budget over an ensemble
confirmed_sources.download_hint: DOI 10.1029/2019WR026604; browser-header curl returns 200. MATLAB reference implementation at https://github.com/hydrophile/WRR-Manuscript-Lake-Mendocino-EFO-Model (7 stars, last push 2020-04-06, 84 MB, NO LICENSE FILE).
confirmed_sources.caveat: The 33% figure is for an optimised risk tolerance curve; the FVA's adopted Modified Hybrid EFO delivers 20%. Do not conflate them. The reference code is MATLAB and unlicensed - not reusable in a Python project without permission.

confirmed_sources.name: Brodeur, Delaney, Whitin & Steinschneider (2024), Synthetic Forecast Ensembles for Evaluating Forecast Informed Reservoir Operations, Water Resources Research
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Directly attacks the problem AquaSync has: you cannot evaluate a forecast-informed policy when you only hold a few years of real forecasts. Generates large synthetic ensembles of hydrologic forecasts with controllable skill so FIRO policies can be stress-tested across far more events than the observational record contains. 18 citations.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the methodologically correct way to test AquaSync's optimiser without a long forecast archive and without assuming perfect foresight
confirmed_sources.download_hint: DOI 10.1029/2023WR034898. Code: https://github.com/zpb4/FIRO_synthetic-ensemble-forecasts (R, 0 stars, last push 2024-01-03, no license) and https://github.com/zpb4/WRR-Manuscript-Lake-Mendocino-EFO-Model (MATLAB, 0 stars, 2023-10-18).
confirmed_sources.caveat: Both companion repos are unlicensed and unstarred - reference implementations, not maintained libraries. Expect to reimplement rather than reuse.

confirmed_sources.name: zpb4/syn-forecast_stochastic - synthetic hydrology and forecast generation with a FIRO model
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The live successor to the 2024 synthetic-ensemble work. Python, MIT licensed, supporting a manuscript titled 'Forecast Informed Reservoir Operations (FIRO) for the future: Exploring the operational implications of climate extremes and evolving forecast skill with large-sample synthetic hydrology and forecasts'. Includes a FIRO model for Lake Oroville.

confirmed_sources.name: Albano et al. (2026), Characterizing Watershed Responses and Reservoir Operational Flexibilities: Analyses to Support FIRO Planning and Assessments, Water Resources Research
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: A transferable screening method for whether FIRO is viable at a given reservoir before committing to a full viability assessment. Defines an 'operational flexibility' metric - how reservoir inflow timing and magnitude relate to available storage space and the maximum safe release rate - which then sets the required forecast lead time. Applied to 32 reservoirs in California and western Nevada; snow-dominated basins have markedly less flexibility than rain-dominated ones and need longer lead times. Uses precipitation amount, phase and soil moisture as runoff-generation mediators with automated baseflow separation. Co-authored with USACE (Forbis, Yeates) and CW3E (Kalansky).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - gives AquaSync a defensible, citable way to answer 'is forecast-informed operation viable at Idukki at all' before claiming any benefit
confirmed_sources.last_activity: published online 10 August 2026; issue dated July 2026

confirmed_sources.name: F. M. Ralph, FIRO briefing to the California Water Commission, 16 April 2025
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Authoritative status of every FIRO pilot as of April 2025: Howard Hanson Dam (Green River, Seattle District), Willamette Valley (14 dams, Portland District), New Bullards Bar (FVA complete), Oroville, Lake Mendocino (FVA complete), Lake Sonoma, Prado Dam (FVA complete), Seven Oaks Dam. Yuba-Feather FIRO Space quantified: 90,000 AF at New Bullards Bar plus 175,000 AF at Oroville = 265,000 AF combined. WY2025 Lake Mendocino operations stored over 10,000 additional acre-feet. 41 atmospheric rivers hit California between 1 Oct 2024 and 14 Mar 2025; in northern California 85% of annual precipitation variance comes from the wettest 5% of days, almost all AR events.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the current programme scoreboard, and the 85%-of-variance-from-5%-of-days statistic is precisely why FIRO works there and may not transfer to a monsoon basin
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl then pdftotext -layout; it is a slide deck with heavy build-slide repetition
confirmed_sources.caveat: Slides, so figures are headline numbers without methodology. Predates the October 2025 WCM signing.

confirmed_sources.name: GAO-16-685: Army Corps of Engineers - Additional Steps Needed for Review and Revision of Water Control Manuals
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The institutional failure mode, documented. USACE operates more than 700 dams. Engineer regulations require water control manual review no less than every 10 years, but the extent of reviews and revisions is unclear because they are neither documented nor tracked. Officials in all 15 districts interviewed said they do not document informal reviews because they consider them part of the daily routine of operating projects. Only 1 of 8 divisions tracked whether water control plans actually reflected real operations. GAO recommended defining what constitutes a review and tracking which manuals need revision; both closed as implemented by November 2018.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the honest answer to 'how do water control manuals get changed': mostly they do not, and until 2018 nobody was tracking it
confirmed_sources.download_hint: gao.gov blocks curl (403 even with full browser headers) but WebFetch reads the product page successfully. PDF nominally at https://www.gao.gov/assets/gao-16-685.pdf (also 403 to curl).
confirmed_sources.caveat: 403 to curl - I read it via WebFetch, not a direct download, so I could not verify page-level detail. Predates the FIRO programme's expansion and does not quantify manual ages.

confirmed_sources.name: Delft-FEWS FAQ (Deltares)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Authoritative licensing statement. Delft-FEWS is available at zero licence cost - you only accept the licence agreement - but it is 'Open Software, but not Open Source': Deltares retains central code control because it runs critical operational systems. Customisation happens through the General Adapter and open API. Users with a support and maintenance agreement receive one release per year; pricing is only via Deltares Services. The companion About page records deployment in over forty operational forecasting centres worldwide since 2002/2003, with adapters for more than 100 information sources and more than 50 simulation modules (HEC, MIKE, HBV, SOBEK named).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the de facto operational platform is free to licence but not forkable, which shapes any AquaSync productisation or integration strategy
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Also https://publicwiki.deltares.nl/spaces/FEWSDOC/pages/149162816/About+Delft-FEWS (200) and https://www.deltares.nl/en/software-and-data/products/delft-fews-platform (200). India pilot documented at https://publicwiki.deltares.nl/display/TKIP/DEL047+-+DAMSAFE+Enhancing+Dam+safety+and+Reservoir+Management+in+India (200).
confirmed_sources.caveat: NO INDIA DEPLOYMENT IS DOCUMENTED on the Deltares pages - countries named are Sudan, Pakistan, Czech Republic, Netherlands, England, Wales, Switzerland, Taiwan. The only India use I could verify is the DAMSAFE pilot at Bhadra dam, Karnataka (Deltares/SkyGeo/Royal Eijkelkamp/iPresas, Netherlands Partners for Water, ~2017-2020) - a pilot, not a CWC-wide operational system, and its project site damsafe.eu is dead (000). Do NOT claim Delft-FEWS is used by CWC; I found no evidence for that.

confirmed_sources.name: UW-SASWE/RAT - Reservoir Assessment Tool 3.0
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The satellite-based reservoir monitoring framework behind the Kerala papers. Estimates surface area, storage change, inflow (VIC hydrological model), outflow, evaporation and area-elevation curves for arbitrary reservoirs. Actively maintained: releases v3.0.17 (2025-04-11), v3.0.18 (2025-08-18), v3.0.19 (2025-11-25).
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - a working, licensed, maintained baseline for satellite-derived Idukki/Idamalayar state that AquaSync could integrate or benchmark against
confirmed_sources.download_hint: gh repo clone UW-SASWE/RAT; global web app and code download also at http://www.satellitedams.net (verified 200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: GPL-3.0 is copyleft - linking RAT into AquaSync imposes GPL obligations on the combined work. Their own paper reports Idukki inflow correlation of only 0.63, and satellite outflow estimates underestimate peak releases badly enough that outflow peaks can vanish entirely.

confirmed_sources.name: SASWE operational Kerala reservoir monitoring instance (RAT 3.0)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Live Kerala deployment of RAT 3.0 with per-reservoir inflow, outflow, surface area, temperature, storage change, area-elevation curve, evaporation and suspended sediment, a Forecast Date selector, and a Download Data section. Developed by Sarath Suresh, SASWE Labs, University of Washington; funded by NASA, KSCSTE (Kerala State Council for Science, Technology and Environment) and CWRDM.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - an existing, funded, Kerala-government-linked operational system covering the same reservoirs; AquaSync needs to know whether it complements or duplicates this
confirmed_sources.license: unstated on the portal; underlying RAT is GPL-3.0
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Explore the Download Data link; underlying engine is UW-SASWE/RAT
confirmed_sources.caveat: Research-lab hosted rather than an official Kerala government service, so continuity depends on grant funding. I did not verify update frequency, forecast horizon, or whether Idukki specifically is included.

confirmed_sources.name: Koo et al. (2025), Balancing Operators' Risk Averseness in Model Predictive Control for Real-time Reservoir Flood Control (arXiv preprint; J. Hydroinformatics 2025)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: States the deployment failure directly: 'optimisation methodologies have not been widely applied in real-time operation due to disparities between research assumptions and practical requirements'. Their Parameterised Dynamic MPC adds practical objectives - minimising the MAGNITUDE AND FREQUENCY OF CHANGES to the existing outflow schedule - and treats operator risk tolerance as a dynamic variable adapting to hydrological conditions rather than a fixed constant. Case study: Daecheong multipurpose reservoir, South Korea.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - AquaSync's optimiser searches over (target level, start hour, max rate) but almost certainly does not penalise gate-schedule churn, which is the objective real operators actually care about
confirmed_sources.license: arXiv preprint; journal version J. Hydroinformatics (2025) jh2025019
confirmed_sources.download_hint: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04506; metadata via export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2407.04506
confirmed_sources.caveat: No code availability stated. Single reservoir in a temperate East Asian monsoon - closer to Kerala than California is, but still not the same regime.

confirmed_sources.name: Rayner, Lach & Ingram (2005), Weather forecasts are for wimps: why water resource managers do not use climate forecasts, Climatic Change 69(2):197-227
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The canonical study of why operators reject forecasts: traditional reliance on large built infrastructure, organisational conservatism and complexity, mismatch of forecast temporal and spatial scales to management needs, political disincentives to innovation, and regulatory constraints. Concludes adoption depends on forecasts being embedded in existing organisational routines and industry codes plus changed management incentives - not on better forecasts.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - twenty years on it still explains why a technically correct optimiser gets ignored, and it predicts exactly the route FIRO took (change the manual, not the operator)
confirmed_sources.caveat: US water utilities, 2005, seasonal climate forecasts rather than short-range flood forecasts. Directionally right, specifics dated. Complement with the NIDIS FIRO barriers workshop at https://www.drought.gov/news/forecast-informed-reservoir-operations-firo-overcoming-barriers-and-realizing-benefits-2019-09 (verified 200), which names prescriptive operations, operator intimidation by available tools, politics and demonstrating value to management.

confirmed_sources.name: Google Flood Forecasting API / Flood Hub
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Operational riverine flood forecasting API: daily hydrologic forecasts to a 7-day horizon plus flood status updated several times a day, over 5,000 verified gauge locations and ~250,000 virtual gauges across 150+ countries. Production model is a Mean Embedding Forecast LSTM as of December 2025. Coverage extended to all of India in partnership with the Central Water Commission, which measures water levels hourly at over a thousand gauges.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the most plausible free route to 7-day forecasts that would let AquaSync replace perfect foresight with a real forecast
confirmed_sources.license: Google API terms; access by application
confirmed_sources.last_activity: live; methodology paper HESS 26:4013 (2022), verified 200; code at https://github.com/google-research/flood-forecasting (328 stars, Apache-2.0, Python, pushed 2026-08-25)
confirmed_sources.download_hint: API FAQ at https://support.google.com/flood-hub/answer/16364206 (verified 200)
confirmed_sources.caveat: I COULD NOT CONFIRM gauge or virtual-gauge coverage on the Periyar specifically, nor whether forecasts exist upstream of Idukki where they would be useful. Flood Hub forecasts river stage/discharge at gauges, not reservoir inflow - converting across a regulated cascade with Mullaperiyar upstream is exactly the hard part. Related: https://www.keralafloodwatch.in/ (verified 200) claims to aggregate IMD, CWC, KSEB, ISRO and Flood Hub feeds for 44 rivers and 81 dams, but its provenance is UNCERTAIN - it is not linked from sdma.kerala.gov.in, so verify its numbers against the KSDMA bulletin before relying on it.

verification_notes: This domain has NOT been through the adversarial verification pass. URLs carry the researching agent's own reported status only. Treat as provisional.

Use the Maharashtra WRD mirror instead - a verified real 459 KB PDF with the correct gazette header.

dead end: damsafety.in/ecm-includes/PDFs/Dam_Safety_Act_2021.pdf returns HTTP 200 but downloads ZERO BYTES. A 200 status code is not proof of content - always check file size and file type after downloading. Same trap in reverse: egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2021/232128.pdf returns 200 and is a genuine 1.5 MB PDF, but its content is an NH22 land-acquisition notification, NOT the Dam Safety Act.

dead end: publications.usace.army.mil blocks everything: er_1110-2-240.pdf and em_1110-2-3600.pdf return 403 to curl with full browser headers AND to WebFetch, from multiple district mirrors (nwd.usace.army.mil also 403). I could not directly read the USACE deviation regulations; the three-category description (planned / unplanned / emergency, with emergency approvable by phone followed by a documented evaluation to the Division Commander, and each Division setting its own minor/major definitions) comes from search-engine indexing only and must be re-verified before quoting in any deliverable.

dead end: gao.gov returns 403 to curl even with a full Chrome UA and Accept headers, but WebFetch reads it fine. The exact reverse holds for sandrp.in, which returns 403 to WebFetch but 200 to curl with a browser UA. Neither tool alone is sufficient - always try both before concluding a source is unreachable.

dead end: India-WRIS (indiawris.gov.in) is completely unreachable from this host: 000 on the root, /wris/, arc.indiawris.gov.in and a POST to /Dataset/Reservoir, with connections hanging rather than refusing. This is the obvious place to look for pre-2020 Indian reservoir time series and I could not test it at all. It may be geo-restricted to India - retest from an Indian network before concluding the historical data does not exist.

dead end: Mishra et al. 'The Kerala flood of 2018' (hess-2018-480) is NOT a peer-reviewed paper. Copernicus status: 'The manuscript was not accepted for further review after discussion.' Much of the 2018-2021 commentary cites it as published, including material that fed the Amicus Curiae report, and the Kerala government has used precisely that error to discredit the whole dam-mismanagement argument. Cite Vegad & Mishra 2025 (npj Natural Hazards, properly published) instead.

dead end: J. Harsha's 'Role of dams in Kerala Floods 2018: What are we missing?' is NOT indexed in Crossref - I searched by author, by title, and within the ISH Journal of Hydraulic Engineering (ISSN 0971-5010) and found nothing. It exists only as a ResearchGate entry and as SANDRP guest articles, because Current Science declined the rebuttal without peer review. There is no citable journal version; cite the SANDRP articles and say so explicitly.

dead end: cw3e.ucsd.edu/firo_lake_mendocino_fva - the URL printed in the official Lake Mendocino one-page summary (February 2021) - is DEAD (404). The live FIRO hub is https://cw3e.ucsd.edu/firo/. Likewise github.com/hydrophile/EFO does not exist; the actual EFO code repo is hydrophile/WRR-Manuscript-Lake-Mendocino-EFO-Model (MATLAB, 7 stars, last push 2020-04-06, 84 MB, and crucially NO LICENSE FILE, so it cannot be legally reused).

dead end: escholarship.org/uc/item/3b63q04n - the recommended citation URL for the Lake Mendocino FVA - returns 202, a Cloudflare interstitial rather than a genuine failure. Do not record it as broken and do not script around it; fetch the PDF directly from cw3e.ucsd.edu. Similarly the 2019 KSDMA 'Orange Book of Disaster Management' (verified 200) is NOT the source of Kerala's dam alert levels despite its reputation - it contains only two lines assigning dam-break and dam-spillway responsibility to KSEB/WR. The blue/orange/red levels come from the CWC/KSEB rule levels in the KSDMA daily bulletin.

dead end: Publisher paywalls that defeat both curl and WebFetch: ascelibrary.org (403 - blocks Das et al. 2025, the closest published competitor, for which I could verify only title/authors/journal/date via Crossref), sciencedirect.com (400/403), and nature.com which issues a 303 to idp.nature.com for automated fetch. For all three the Crossref REST API (api.crossref.org/works/<DOI>) reliably returns title, authors, date, citation count and often a full abstract. Beware UnicodeEncodeError on Windows cp1252 when printing its output - wrap stdout in a UTF-8 TextIOWrapper.

dimensions.dimension: Integrating with existing dam, SCADA and government water systems (KSEB / KSDMA / CWC / NDSA), industrial protocols, open water-data standards, Dam Safety Act 2021 compliance, and cybersecurity constraints

confirmed_sources.name: KSEB Dam Safety Organisation - Monthly Statistics (daily reservoir water levels, 91 Excel workbooks)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 91 monthly .xlsx/.xls workbooks 'Water level of main reservoirs of KSEB Limited', Jan 2019 to Jul 2026, one sheet per day (sometimes 3-hourly during floods). Download pattern https://dams.kseb.in/?wpdmdl=<ID>, IDs 310 (Jan 2019) to 6380 (Jul 2026). Modern schema (Jul 2026): Sl.No | Reservoir | District | FRL | Rule level | Water level | MWL | Spillway Crest Level | Blue/Orange/Red Alert level | Live Storage at FRL (MCM) | Live Storage (MCM) | %Storage | Inflow (MCM). 2019 schema adds a 'Previous Year Water Level' column.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - authoritative primary KSEB source for Idukki and Idamalayar, starts 14 months before the amith-vp GitHub feed (2020-08-13), covers the corrupt 2020-09-25 to 2021-04-30 window with clean data, and its 2019 previous-year column yields ~100 days of genuine 2018 levels
confirmed_sources.license: Government of Kerala / KSEB Ltd public download, no explicit licence stated
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A "Mozilla/5.0" -OJ "https://dams.kseb.in/?wpdmdl=315"  (June 2019.xlsx, 1,511,065 bytes). Loop IDs 315,500..505 then 506..6380 from the page HTML.
confirmed_sources.caveat: IDs 310-314 (Jan-May 2019) 302-redirect to http://kseboa.in/... which does not resolve (curl 000) - those five months are UNAVAILABLE. Aug-2019 (id 501) and Sep-2019 (id 502) workbooks are incomplete (10 and 9 sheets) so the 2018 previous-year series has a hole across 01-19 Aug 2018 - the flood peak days. Files are .xls for some 2021-2022 months (needs xlrd) and .xlsx otherwise (needs openpyxl); neither was installed in this environment, I parsed the OOXML by hand with zipfile+ElementTree.

confirmed_sources.name: KSEB monthly workbook, June 2019 (worked example / proof of 2018 data)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 31 sheets: 'Sheet1 (2)' plus 01.06.19 to 30.06.19. Header row: SL NO | RESERVOIR | MWL (m) | FRL (m) | Crest Level (m) | Present Water Level (m) | Previous Year Water Level | Percentage Storage | Rainfall (mm) | Generation (Mu) | Spill (cumecs). Verified values on the 01.06.19 sheet: IDAMALAYAR present 126.25 m / previous-year 129.58 m; IDUKKI present 2314.64 ft / previous-year 2323.24 ft.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the concrete proof that KSEB workbooks carry a same-date previous-year column, i.e. the mechanism that recovers 2018 Idukki/Idamalayar levels
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A "Mozilla/5.0" -o june2019.xlsx "https://dams.kseb.in/?wpdmdl=315"
confirmed_sources.caveat: Idukki levels are in FEET in these sheets, Idamalayar in METRES - mixed units within one row set. Kuttiyadi rows show an obvious data-entry error (MWL 758.04 vs FRL 2487) so per-row unit sanity checks are mandatory.

confirmed_sources.name: KSEB Ltd live dam water level dashboard
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: HTML table, 17 columns, all KSEB reservoirs: Today's Water level (m), Today's Live Storage (MCM), %Storage wrt Live Storage at FRL, Same day previous year Water level (m), Same day previous year Live Storage (MCM), Inflow (MU), Rainfall (mm), Blue level, Orange level, Red Level, MWL, FRL, Spillway Crest Level, Live Storage at FRL (MCM), Remarks. Accepts ?date=YYYY-MM-DD.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the only free source I verified that publishes the seasonally varying Blue/Orange/Red alert bands AquaSync's policy search must honour, and it confirms Idukki Live Storage at FRL = 1459.49 MCM
confirmed_sources.license: KSEB Ltd public web page, no licence stated
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L --globoff -A "Mozilla/5.0" "https://kseb.in/dashboard/view/waterlevel?date=2026-08-20" then parse <tr> rows
confirmed_sources.caveat: Archive is SHALLOW. Verified rows for 2026-08-01, 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-26; empty for 2026-07-01 and every earlier date I tried back to 2018. The DD-MM-YYYY format the form's own <input type=date> emits returns nothing - only ISO YYYY-MM-DD works. It is a rolling window, so scrape daily.

confirmed_sources.name: Kerala State Load Despatch Centre - System Statistics: Storage
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Daily reservoir table with columns MDDL (m) | FRL (m) | Effective Storage at FRL (mcm) | Gen. Capability at FRL (mu) | Reservoir | Level (m) | Effective Storage (mcm) | Storage (%) | Gen. Capability gross (mu) | Gen. Capability station (mu) | Rainfall (mm) | Spill | INFLOW (mcm/day) | Cum. inflow for month (MU) | Previous day's storage (%) | Remarks. Verified 25.08.2026: Idukki inflow 29.734 mcm/day, Idamalayar 2.61 mcm/day.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - free daily OBSERVED INFLOW for exactly AquaSync's two reservoirs, the variable the perfect-foresight optimiser currently assumes it knows
confirmed_sources.license: KSEB/Kerala SLDC public page, no licence stated
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A "Mozilla/5.0" "https://sldckerala.com/index.php?id=7" then parse <tr>/<td>
confirmed_sources.caveat: HISTORICAL RETRIEVAL DOES NOT WORK. The page carries a POST form (action=index.php, hidden txtDate=943900200, submit name=sbtstore) and a calendar iframe writing date1. I tried POSTing txtDate as a unix timestamp and date1 in several formats to both index.php and index.php?id=7 - the header always came back 'STORAGE AS ON 25.08.2026'. Treat as a forward-only daily snapshot. Also sldckerala.com is not a gov.in domain; confirm provenance before citing it in a formal deliverable.

confirmed_sources.name: KSDMA - Dam Water Level (daily consolidated KSEB + Irrigation bulletins)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Two daily PDFs - 'Water Levels of Major Reservoirs (KSEB)' and '(Irrigation)' - updated daily at 11:00 IST, plus a guidelines document on how to read the tables.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - this is the official disaster-management-side view of the same numbers, and it is what KSDMA staff actually look at; matching AquaSync's outputs to this document's fields is the fastest route to being legible to KSDMA
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L "https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/dam-water-level/" then follow the two PDF links
confirmed_sources.caveat: PDF ONLY - no CSV, no JSON, no API. Requires PDF table extraction. Combines KSEB (hydel) and Irrigation Department reservoirs in separate documents with different schemas.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC - Study Report: Kerala Floods of August 2018 (Hydrological Studies Organisation, Sept 2018)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 48 pp, 6.0 MB, fully text-extractable. Hourly narrative of Idukki reservoir operation 09-18 Aug 2018 (levels, spill, powerhouse release, peak inflow 2532 cumec at 22:00 on 15 Aug, 41% attenuation, FRL touched 01:00 on 17 Aug); Idamalayar operation (168.06 m on 8 Aug, peak inflow 1164 cumec on 16 Aug, average spill 1271 cumec, no attenuation); Neeleswaram G&D peak 8,800 cumec at 14:00-15:00 on 16 Aug 2018 at EL 12.4 m; Periyar drainage area 4,033 km2 to Neeleswaram, Mullaperiyar->Idukki free catchment 605 km2, Idamalayar catchment 472 km2; sub-basin rainfall depths for 15-17 Aug 2018 (Periyar 588 mm) compared against the 1924 Devikulam storm; Annex-I water level plots for CWC G&D sites.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the single best verified source of 2018 Idukki/Idamalayar operational data AND the downstream gauge (Neeleswaram) that Muskingum must be calibrated against
confirmed_sources.license: Government of India / CWC, published by KSDMA
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A "Mozilla/5.0" -o cwc_kerala_2018.pdf "https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/CWC-Report-on-Kerala-Floods.pdf" then pypdf extract_text
confirmed_sources.caveat: The hourly inflow/outflow/level series exist only as CHART IMAGES (Fig.4, Fig.5, Fig.3) - the PDF text layer preserves the axis tick labels (confirming hourly resolution and the 09-08-18 12:00 to 18-08-18 06:00 span) but NOT the plotted values. Recovering the series needs chart digitisation. CWC's own Limitation (ii) states gauge records at some G&D sites could not be observed on 16-17 Aug 2018 due to site inaccessibility, so the 8,800 cumec peak is partly estimated.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC - Report on Kerala Flood & Solutions (December 2018)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: 60 pp, 9.7 MB, text-extractable. MIKE FLOOD / MIKE 11 2-D hydrodynamic modelling of Periyar, Pamba, Chalakudy and the Vembanad Lake catchment. Sec 7.1 MIKE 11 calibration at Neeleswaram. Sec 8.3.2.2: CWC proposes level forecasting at Neeleswaram from combined Idukki + Idamalayar discharges with a TRAVEL TIME OF 8 HOURS; Neeleswaram stage-discharge curve and cross-section give Warning Level 9 m, Danger Level 10 m; intervening-catchment unit hydrograph from ~12 IMD daily rain gauges. Sec 8.1 return-period-based inundation maps. Sec 8.4 water-level prediction downstream of any dam. States Idukki has released water on only three occasions ever: 1988, 1992, 2018.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - gives an officially published 8-hour Idukki+Idamalayar to Neeleswaram travel time (a direct calibration anchor for Muskingum K) and is the government's own precedent for 2D inundation on the Periyar
confirmed_sources.license: Government of India / CWC, published by KSDMA
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L -A "Mozilla/5.0" -o cwc_kerala_dec2018.pdf "https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/Kerala_28122018_CWC_December-2018.pdf"
confirmed_sources.caveat: CWC explicitly notes 'the hourly dam inflow/outflow through rivers were not yet received from the project authorities' - so even CWC modelled Idukki/Idamalayar outflow with MIKE-11 rather than using KSEB's actual hourly records. Correlation curves and travel-time tables are figures, not tabulated numbers. Only 2018 was analysed for the Periyar reach.

confirmed_sources.name: Encardio Rite - Idukki Dam monitoring case study (the incumbent SHM/EWS system)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Names the contract - 'Real-Time Early Warning Structure Health Monitoring and Data Interpretation (RESHMI)' under DRIP - and the stack: geotechnical + geodetic sensors (prism targets on the downstream intrados read by two robotic total stations with in-house control boxes), a weather station (air temp, wind speed/direction, RH, solar radiation, barometric pressure, rain gauge), seismic sensors, compact data loggers with DAS + interface unit + BusMux, GSM/GPRS modem transmission to a central server, and the proprietary 'Drishti' database management system.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - defines the actual technical boundary at Idukki: there is no open protocol endpoint, the integration is a vendor database export
confirmed_sources.license: vendor marketing content, all rights reserved
confirmed_sources.download_hint: WebFetch or curl the page directly
confirmed_sources.caveat: Vendor marketing, not a spec sheet: gives NO instrument COUNTS, no installation date, no protocol version, no sampling rate. Cross-check against DRIP documentation before quoting. The companion press piece (https://magazine.watertoday.org/news/national/early-warning-system-installed-on-idukki-dam, verified 200) adds that data goes to the KSEB monitoring station at Pallam, Kottayam and the dam monitoring & research station at Vazhathoppe, Idukki.

confirmed_sources.name: NDSA - Regulations notified under the Dam Safety Act 2021 (all 20)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The complete notified regulation set with publish dates. The four that bind AquaSync: Reg 1 (13/03/2024) log books/database under s.18; Reg 5 (13/04/2024) EAP update interval under s.36(1)(b); Reg 8 (24/04/2024) minimum instrumentation sets and manner of installation under s.32(1); Reg 16 (20/05/2024) data requirements of hydro-meteorological stations under s.33(1); Reg 9 (24/04/2025) form, manner and time interval for forwarding the analysis of readings to the State Dam Safety Organisation under s.32(2). Also Reg 6 mandatory review of design flood under s.38(2)(b), Reg 12 risk assessment interval under s.35(2), Reg 18 vulnerability and hazard classification under s.17.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - this is the statutory basis for pitching AquaSync's telemetry layer as a compliance aid rather than a nice-to-have
confirmed_sources.download_hint: The site is a React SPA - the human route is /documents/dame-safety-act-regulation (note the 'dame' typo in the real route). For machine access see the API row below.
confirmed_sources.caveat: The /documents/dam-safety-act-regulations spelling ALSO returns 200 but renders an empty shell; the working route is 'dame-safety-act-regulation'. WebFetch on either returns only the page header because the content is client-rendered.

confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: GET returns the document-type map: {guidelines, reports, order-and-notice, regulation} with frontendRoute/apiKey/apiEndpoint. Then POST https://ndsa.gov.in/ndsa-backend/web/regulation?lang=en with body {"page":0,"sort":"","search":""} returns {regulations:[{title, publish_date, due_date, pdf_title, pdf_link, ...}], pagination:{total_count:20, page_size:10, total_pages:2}}. Same pattern for guidelines / reports / order-and-notice.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - machine-readable, no auth, gives every Dam Safety Act regulation PDF link programmatically so AquaSync can track new notifications automatically
confirmed_sources.license: Government of India public data, no licence stated
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"page":0,"sort":"","search":""}' "https://ndsa.gov.in/ndsa-backend/web/regulation?lang=en"

DRIP Phase I (2012-2021) covered 223 dams across 7 states INCLUDING KERALA. DRIP II & III operationalised Oct 2021, outlay Rs 10,211 crore (World Bank + AIIB), 736 dams / 19 states / 3 central agencies. Act mandates 'Inflow Forecasting, Early Warning System, Integrated Operation of Reservoirs'.

IEC 62443 is the referenced OT baseline.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC - Flood Forecasting / Hydrological Observation
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The national flood-forecast network: 325 forecast stations covering 197 low-lying areas/cities/towns plus 128 RESERVOIRS, across 20 river basins; 878 hydrological and hydro-meteorological sites operated by CWC for gauge, discharge, sediment and water quality; ~1,054 telemetry-equipped stations. Data transmitted by wireless, telephone/mobile, VSAT and satellite telemetry. Inflow forecasts at the 128 reservoirs are provided to assist project authorities in reservoir regulation.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - establishes the ADVISORY posture (CWC forecasts assist, the dam owner decides) that AquaSync should adopt verbatim, and confirms Neeleswaram/Vandiperiyar exist as CWC hydrological observation stations on the Periyar
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L "https://cwc.gov.in/flood-forecasting-hydrological-observation"
confirmed_sources.caveat: Narrative page, no station list download, no API. It does NOT confirm whether any Periyar station is a FORECAST station (as opposed to an observation station) - the Dec-2018 CWC report suggests Kerala forecast stations were still being proposed at that time.

confirmed_sources.name: CWC Advisory Flood Forecast (AFF) - methodology
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: AFF methodology: coupled hydrologic (rainfall-runoff) plus hydrodynamic river models; 20 river basin models covering the CWC flood forecasting network; models re-run EVERY THREE HOURS day and night; SEVEN-DAY lead time; inputs are satellite and rain-gauge observed rainfall plus IMD GFS and WRF forecast rainfall, river cross-sections, historical discharge and water level, bathymetry.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the operational template for how a government-accepted advisory forecast is described, run and caveated in India; also the concrete 3-hourly / 7-day cadence AquaSync's forecast layer should aim to match or beat
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L "https://aff.india-water.gov.in/method.php"
confirmed_sources.caveat: Portal is labelled Beta. No Kerala or Periyar mention on the methodology page - AFF's 20 basin models may not include the Periyar. No public API. The page's own caveat: 'the accuracy of the model is limited by the quality of data available.' Companion operational portal https://ffs.india-water.gov.in/ verified 200 but is a Kendo/Angular SPA with no exposed JSON endpoint in its served HTML.

confirmed_sources.name: OGC SensorThings API Part 1: Sensing, Version 1.1 (OGC 18-088)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The full Implementation Standard: OData-derived REST model with Thing / Location / Datastream / Sensor / ObservedProperty / Observation / FeatureOfInterest entities, full CRUD, $expand/$filter/$select query options, and MQTT extension for publish/subscribe on observations.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - the right standard IF an agency partner demands sensor-observation interoperability; the MQTT extension is the natural bridge from a Sparkplug B edge to a standards-compliant store
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L "https://docs.ogc.org/is/18-088/18-088.html"
confirmed_sources.caveat: NOT adopted by India-WRIS, NHP, CWC or KSDMA - adopting it buys international interoperability, not Indian integration. The data model fits OBSERVATIONS well and model FORECASTS badly; use EDR for forecast output.

confirmed_sources.name: OGC API - Environmental Data Retrieval Standard (OGC 19-086r6)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Lightweight query interface family (position, radius, area, cube, trajectory, corridor, items, locations, instances) for spatio-temporal data - designed exactly for asking 'give me the time series at this point for this window' against gridded or model output.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - the lowest-effort way to make AquaSync's reservoir-level, discharge and inundation output machine-consumable by any agency, via pygeoapi
confirmed_sources.download_hint: curl -s -L "https://docs.ogc.org/is/19-086r6/19-086r6.html"
confirmed_sources.caveat: Standards conformance is worth nothing on its own if no Indian counterparty consumes EDR - and none currently does. Justify it as future-proofing plus a clean internal API, not as an integration deliverable.

confirmed_sources.name: pygeoapi
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Python server implementing the OGC API suite (Features, Coverages, Tiles, Records, Processes, EDR) with a plugin provider mechanism; deploys as a Flask/Starlette app over an existing data source.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - pure Python, MIT, drops into AquaSync's existing stack, ~1-2 days to a working OGC API - EDR endpoint over the model's time series
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install pygeoapi==0.24.0  (requires Python >=3.12)
confirmed_sources.caveat: 0.24.0 requires Python >=3.12 - check AquaSync's interpreter before committing. 40 open issues. You must write an EDR provider plugin for your own data model; the shipped providers cover files/PostGIS/xarray, not a bespoke reservoir model.

confirmed_sources.name: FROST-Server (Fraunhofer IOSB) - OGC SensorThings reference implementation
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: The first complete open-source official reference implementation of the OGC SensorThings API, with a plugin system that can extend or replace the data model; ships as Docker images (fraunhoferiosb/frost-server on Docker Hub).
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium - use only if a counterparty mandates SensorThings conformance; otherwise it is a Java+PostGIS operational burden beside a Python system
confirmed_sources.download_hint: docker pull fraunhoferiosb/frost-server ; Python client: pip install frost-sta-client==1.1.53
confirmed_sources.caveat: Java + PostgreSQL/PostGIS + Docker - a whole second runtime. 86 open issues. The Python client frost-sta-client (LGPL3, 1.1.53, released 2025-09-19) is maintained separately and less actively than the server.

confirmed_sources.name: pymodbus
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Full Modbus implementation in Python - client, server and simulator, sync and async APIs, TCP/RTU/ASCII/TLS.
confirmed_sources.relevance: low for KSEB integration, high as a bench tool - Modbus is not how a dam SCADA in India exposes data northbound, but individual loggers and sensors often speak it
confirmed_sources.license: BSD-3-Clause (GitHub metadata says NOASSERTION; PyPI declares BSD-3-Clause)
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install pymodbus==3.15.0  (requires Python >=3.10)
confirmed_sources.caveat: Modbus carries no timestamp, no quality flag and no authentication. Anything you read has the poll time, not the measurement time - unacceptable for a flood record. Zero open issues on the repo (aggressively triaged), which can mask unresolved questions.

confirmed_sources.name: opcua-asyncio (asyncua)
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Async Python OPC-UA client and server: browsing, subscriptions, historical data access, method calls, security policies and certificate handling.
confirmed_sources.relevance: high - OPC-UA is the realistic read-only northbound boundary a modern SCADA/EMS will expose, and Kerala SLDC has a sanctioned SCADA/EMS replacement at Kalamassery that will offer it
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install asyncua==2.0.1  (requires Python >=3.10)
confirmed_sources.caveat: LGPL-3.0 - fine as an imported library in a service, needs review if AquaSync is ever statically linked or shipped. 244 open issues. The 2.x major bump (June 2026) may contain breaking API changes versus tutorials written for 1.x. Getting certificates and a Basic256Sha256 policy working against a real utility server is where the schedule risk lives, not the Python.

confirmed_sources.name: iec104-python / c104 (Fraunhofer FIT) - IEC 60870-5-104 in Python
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Object-oriented Python module wrapping lib60870-C to simulate and speak IEC 60870-5-104 as SCADA master or RTU, with state structures and Python callback handlers.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium-high - IEC 101/104 is the protocol family Indian transmission-level SCADA actually uses (not DNP3), so this is the correct client if KSEB ever offers a direct RTU-level monitor-direction feed
confirmed_sources.download_hint: pip install c104==2.2.1  (requires Python >=3.7)
confirmed_sources.caveat: GPL-3.0 IS A REAL BLOCKER if AquaSync is ever distributed rather than operated as a service - and the underlying mz-automation/lib60870 (592 stars, pushed 2026-07-15) is GPL-3.0 too, with a commercial licence available from MZ Automation. PyPI release is ~16 months behind the repo. IEC-104 has no native authentication; IEC 62351 security is a bolt-on rarely deployed in India. 22 open issues.

confirmed_sources.name: libiec61850 (MZ Automation) - IEC 61850 including the -7-410 hydro profile
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: C implementation of IEC 61850 client/server (MMS, GOOSE, Sampled Values) - the substrate for IEC 61850-7-410, which defines the logical nodes and data objects for hydropower plants (gates, turbines, reservoirs).
confirmed_sources.relevance: low today, strategic later - nothing at Idukki speaks IEC 61850, but -7-410 is the only standard that would eventually let a dam expose reservoir and gate state semantically rather than as raw registers
confirmed_sources.download_hint: git clone https://github.com/mz-automation/libiec61850 ; no first-class Python binding - budget C/pybind11 work
confirmed_sources.caveat: GPL-3.0 with the same distribution problem as lib60870. No maintained Python binding. 243 open issues. Documented IEC 61850 hydro deployments are dominated by Spain (>10 projects); Indian hydro adoption is not evidenced in anything I could verify.

confirmed_sources.name: Eclipse Tahu - MQTT Sparkplug B reference implementations
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Reference client libraries and compatible implementations for the Eclipse Sparkplug specification (currently v3.0), defining MQTT topic namespace, protobuf payload encoding, birth/death certificates and device state management for industrial telemetry.
confirmed_sources.relevance: medium-high for AquaSync's OWN edge devices (a stage sensor at Neeleswaram, a Kochi tide gauge) over unreliable GPRS - Sparkplug's birth/death and state-of-health semantics are exactly what the Encardio GSM/GPRS failure mode needs
confirmed_sources.download_hint: Spec PDF (verified 200): https://sparkplug.eclipse.org/specification/version/3.0/documents/sparkplug-specification-3.0.0.pdf ; Python: pip install pysparkplug==0.6.1
confirmed_sources.caveat: Tahu itself is JAVA-centric (language=Java). The Python option, matteosox/pysparkplug, is a single-maintainer project - 24 stars, last push 2025-05-10, PyPI 0.6.1 released 2025-05-10, Apache-2.0, Python >=3.9. Thin bus factor; read the code before depending on it. Sparkplug cannot be applied to KSEB's existing SCADA without KSEB's active participation.
